servers.tagline: D-ID's hosted MCP connecting agents to the D-ID API and docs for avatar video.
servers.description: D-ID hosts an official remote MCP server on its developer docs that lets MCP clients interact with the D-ID API and its documentation for talking-avatar and Agents workflows. D-ID also publishes llms.txt for agent consumption.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http d-id https://docs.d-id.com/mcp

auth.key_url: https://docs.d-id.com/docs/api-keys (D-ID Studio; credits required for API calls)

servers.notes: Docs-platform-hosted (ReadMe-powered) remote MCP; endpoint and setup text re-confirmed unchanged on 2026-09-09, and the exact tool list is still not published openly — D-ID describes the surface only as API access, docs search, live account data and code generation. Auth is whatever your client can send: D-ID's own guidance is that you pass API credentials as headers or query parameters through the MCP client, so there is no OAuth flow and no standard env var. Manage expectations about what a docs-platform MCP is — it is closer to a documentation copilot with API reach than a purpose-built generation server, and nothing about the tool surface is contractual. Landscape note: Synthesia still has no official MCP (only marginal community wrappers and generic Zapier/viaSocket gateways).

servers.name: DaVinci Resolve AI Bridge MCP
servers.tagline: Local MCP bridge into DaVinci Resolve that runs on the Free edition, not just Studio.
servers.description: A Python bridge that starts from Resolve's own Workspace → Scripts menu and hands an MCP client some forty-five tools: timeline inspection, media import and placement, clip transforms and Fusion zoom animation, grade reads and writes, silence detection with marker-then-apply cuts, review on duplicate timelines, and render queueing. It was built Free-first: it runs inside Resolve as a menu script rather than attaching through Studio-only external scripting, so no Studio key is needed. The larger davinci-resolve server now reaches the Free edition the same way, which makes this the lighter, narrower alternative — fewer tools, one Python runtime, and a review-on-a-duplicate-timeline habit baked into the edit tools.

auth.key_url: No key. Requires DaVinci Resolve (Free or Studio) open with a project, Python 3.10+, and the bridge started once per session from Workspace → Scripts → Resolve AI Bridge → Start AI Bridge.

servers.notes: Verified 2026-09-15 against the repo and npm: MIT, v1.12.0 published 7 Sep 2026, ~23 stars, one maintainer on a personal account created June 2026, repo created July 2026 — young, and the submission came from that maintainer. The npx line is an installer, not the server: it creates ~/.resolve-ai-bridge with a private Python environment, adds the Resolve menu entries and merges MCP config into the clients it detects; the stdio server it registers is a local Python command, with `npx -y davinci-resolve-ai-bridge-mcp --serve` as the alternative. Weigh it against davinci-resolve (2.6k stars, 36 compound tools, also Free-capable since its own in-app bridge shipped) and against Resolve Studio 21.1, whose first-party AI-assistant integration is Studio-only. Read the fine print: the README's live-tested matrix is macOS / Resolve Free 21.0.3.7 / Python 3.14.6 only, Windows and Linux are marked as still needing verification, and Studio-only effects stay Studio-only. FFmpeg is an optional extra download for source-frame capture. Tool names above come from the README's tool table, not a live tools/list.

servers.name: DaVinci Resolve MCP
servers.tagline: Full AI control of DaVinci Resolve Studio — edit, grade, Fusion, and render via scripting.
servers.description: MCP server built on Resolve's official Scripting API covering project management, media pool, timeline editing, color grading, Fusion comps, Fairlight audio, and the render queue. The most mature NLE MCP available — a filmmaker-agent can conform timelines, apply grades, and kick off renders without touching the GUI.

auth.key_url: Requires DaVinci Resolve 18.5+ running locally — Studio with External Scripting set to Local, or the free edition through the project's in-app bridge script

servers.notes: Blackmagic is now in this lane itself. Resolve 21.1 shipped 8 Sep 2026, and Blackmagic's own download description says DaVinci Resolve Studio 21.1 'adds new individual MultiMaster trims on the color page, integration with AI assistants and 20 new scripting APIs with built-in console support' — the free 21.1 description says nothing of the kind, so first-party agent control is Studio-only. It is now listed here as davinci-resolve-studio, with the sourcing limits spelled out in that entry — Blackmagic still publishes no fetchable setup page, endpoint or tool list. If you are on Studio 21.1, try the built-in path before installing anything below. The community server remains the option for the free edition and for older Resolve builds. 2,592 stars, MIT, v2.223.0 released 9 Sep 2026 — the most actively maintained NLE MCP in this directory, and now shipping many releases a day. The Studio-only wall has come down: Blackmagic still gates external scripting to Studio, but the project ships an in-app bridge that runs from Resolve's ungated Workspace > Scripts menu, so free-edition users can reach the MCP too. Resolve 18.5+ on macOS, Windows or Linux; Python 3.10-3.12 is the low-risk range (3.13/3.14 work on recent Resolve builds and can fail on older ones). The README claims full coverage of the official scripting API across 36 compound tools (353 granular), 93.6% live-tested against Resolve 19.1.3, 20.3.2 and 21.0.3 — that number is the maintainer's, not ours. macOS gotcha: Resolve only looks for Python in PYTHON3HOME or /usr/local/bin/python3, so Homebrew installs need a launchctl fix. tools_sample is null because the exposed tool list tracks Resolve's scripting API and moves between releases — read tools/list rather than trusting a cached name.

servers.name: DaVinci Resolve Studio MCP (Blackmagic)
servers.tagline: First-party MCP server built into DaVinci Resolve Studio 21.1 — no third-party bridge.
servers.description: Blackmagic shipped agent control as a product feature in Resolve Studio 21.1 (8 Sep 2026): the NLE hosts its own MCP server and configures the client for you from inside the app, so an assistant can read a project, organize media, cut, grade, adjust settings and batch render through Resolve scripting without a community bridge in the path. For anyone already paying for Studio this is the shortest route from agent to timeline, and the first one whose lifecycle is tied to Resolve releases rather than a maintainer.

install.stdio_command: Configured inside the app, not from a shell: in DaVinci Resolve Studio 21.1 choose File > Setup AI Assistants, and Resolve detects supported assistants and writes its own MCP server config into them.

auth.key_url: Requires DaVinci Resolve Studio 21.1 or later — a paid licence via dongle, Blackmagic Cloud licence or activation code — running locally. The free edition of 21.1 does not include it.

servers.notes: Listed 20 Sep 2026 after Blackmagic's own release text finally confirmed the feature: the download description for DaVinci Resolve Studio 21.1 (8 Sep 2026) says it 'adds new individual MultiMaster trims on the color page, integration with AI assistants and 20 new scripting APIs with built-in console support', while the free 21.1 description says nothing of the kind — which is the paywall, in the vendor's own words. Read the sourcing carefully before you trust the details. Blackmagic publishes no web setup page, no endpoint and no tool list; the only first-party documentation is the 183 MB Resolve 21.1 Reference Manual PDF linked above, which we confirmed exists but could not read in this environment. The File > Setup AI Assistants menu path, the named clients (Claude, Claude Code, ChatGPT Codex) and the widely repeated figure of 88 tools all come from that manual as reported consistently by trade coverage, not from a page we fetched — verify them in your own copy of Resolve before relying on them. Same caveat on the report that 21.1 moved Python scripting out of the free edition: if that holds, it also undercuts the free-edition workarounds the community servers rely on, so check your Resolve build before assuming those still work. We have no live tools/list, hence a null tools_sample. Practical comparison: davinci-resolve (samuelgursky) is far better documented, covers Resolve 18.5+ including older builds, and is the option if you are not on Studio 21.1; davinci-resolve-ai-bridge is the lighter Free-first alternative. This entry exists because first-party support changes the maintenance risk, not because it is the richer toolset.

servers.name: Deepgram MCP
servers.tagline: Official Deepgram server: Nova transcription, diarization, and audio intelligence.
servers.description: Deepgram's official MCP server gives agents access to its speech platform — fast, accurate transcription with speaker diarization plus audio-intelligence features. Its tool list is fetched from Deepgram's API at runtime rather than hardcoded, so new capabilities appear without a package upgrade. For film work it handles dailies, interview transcription, and dialogue logging at production scale.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add deepgram -e DEEPGRAM_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY -- deepgram-mcp
install.stdio_command: deepgram-mcp (after `pip install deepgram-mcp`; also bundled with the Deepgram CLI, where `dg mcp` wraps it)

auth.key_url: https://console.deepgram.com (free signup credit)

servers.notes: Official but thin on the ground, and re-checked on 28 Sep 2026 and the code has not moved: PyPI deepgram-mcp still 0.1.1 (4 Apr 2026, its only release), repo still last pushed 6 May 2026, MIT, two stars, eight open issues and climbing. Deepgram's own summary calls it a 'standalone MCP proxy… remote-proxy architecture with zero client upgrades', which is the honest framing — the package is a thin shim and the capability lives upstream. The runtime tool fetch is genuinely useful but means you cannot see the tool surface before connecting, and it depends on Deepgram's developer API at https://api.dx.deepgram.com staying up. An SSE HTTP mode exists: `deepgram-mcp --transport sse --port 8000`. AssemblyAI's only official MCP is a documentation server, not transcription, so Deepgram remains the strongest official cloud-STT MCP.

servers.name: Descript MCP
servers.tagline: Descript's official hosted MCP — import media, run Underlord edits, publish, from your agent.
servers.description: Descript's first-party remote MCP server hands an agent the transcript-based editor: import media from a URL or local file with automatic transcription, then drive Underlord to strip filler words, apply Studio Sound, generate captions, build scenes and highlight reels, or create a whole project from a prompt. It also finds and organizes projects and compositions and publishes to a shareable Descript link. The natural home for interview, doc and podcast-adjacent cutting, where the edit is really a text edit.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http descript https://api.descript.com/v2/mcp

auth.key_url: OAuth via your Descript login — no API token; the connection binds to whichever Descript drive your browser session is in

servers.notes: Re-verified 18 Sep 2026: the overview doc is unchanged and api.descript.com/v2/mcp answers 401 to an anonymous request, so the endpoint is live and auth-gated as listed. Official and hosted, so nothing to install, but the export story is still the catch: Descript documents no rendered media download without publishing — an agent can publish to a Descript web link or hand off a signed URL, and anything else you fetch by exporting from the app yourself. TRANSCRIPTS are the exception, and this run pinned down the formats: text, Markdown, HTML, RTF and SRT come back over MCP, DOCX does not. The docs also cover job tracking and cancellation, which matters because imports and Underlord runs are async. Other documented limits: YouTube URLs cannot be imported, job history is kept 30 days, one connection sees exactly one drive (switching drives means re-authenticating, and editing a project on another drive errors), and Claude's directory connector excludes the generative image/video tools. API and MCP access is included for paying subscribers at no extra cost but every import and Underlord edit burns your plan's media minutes and AI credits. Note the two auth stories: MCP is OAuth through your Descript login with no token, while the REST API uses drive-scoped tokens from Settings → API Tokens — descript.com/api blurs them together. Tool names are still not published, so this entry lists capabilities rather than inventing them.

servers.name: Dropbox MCP Server
servers.tagline: Dropbox's official remote MCP (beta) for dailies, footage folders, and file ops.
servers.description: Dropbox's hosted MCP server (beta) connects agents to Dropbox files and folders with OAuth: list, search, upload, download, move, copy, delete, and share, plus revision history, transcription, and Markdown conversion for drafting and summarization. Supports Dynamic Client Registration for trusted clients like Claude and Cursor.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http dropbox https://mcp.dropbox.com/mcp

auth.key_url: Dropbox OAuth consent via mcp.dropbox.com

servers.notes: Endpoint unchanged on re-check and still beta — Dropbox's beta terms apply on top of your plan. The help page (last revised 18 Mar 2026) now names its tools individually under 'Available tools' instead of the old '25+ tools' gesture, so tools_sample above is quoted from Dropbox rather than guessed; the full set also covers file requests, restore events, usage and quota, and DownloadLink. Dynamic Client Registration only covers a curated client list (Claude Code, Claude web, Cursor, ChatGPT web and Codex); everyone else creates a Dropbox app and configures OAuth 2 redirect URIs by hand, and those access tokens are short-lived enough that you will regenerate them. Change your Dropbox app scopes and you must reconnect the server. A separate official Dash MCP covers enterprise search (dropbox/mcp-server-dash, 10 stars, pushed 30 Jun 2026). The community Go alternative ngs/dropbox-mcp-server has had no commit since Sep 2025 — use the hosted server instead.

servers.name: ElevenLabs MCP
servers.tagline: Official ElevenLabs server: TTS, voice cloning, SFX, music, and dialogue isolation.
servers.description: The official ElevenLabs MCP exposes the full audio platform: text-to-speech with thousands of voices, voice cloning and design, text-to-sound-effects, Eleven Music composition, transcription, and audio isolation, plus video_to_music to score an existing cut and inpainting to replace a section of a generated track. For a filmmaker-agent it covers dialogue, SFX, and score from one connection — the most complete one-stop audio MCP for a film pipeline. ElevenLabs archived the local stdio server in September 2026 and now ships this as a hosted OAuth endpoint.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http elevenlabs https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/mcp
install.stdio_command: uvx elevenlabs-mcp (archived local server; needs ELEVENLABS_API_KEY in the environment)

auth.key_url: Browser OAuth against your ElevenLabs account — no key to rotate; the archived local server still takes ELEVENLABS_API_KEY from the elevenlabs.io dashboard

servers.notes: This entry flipped to the hosted endpoint in September 2026, and the reason is blunt: ElevenLabs archived the local server. github.com/elevenlabs/elevenlabs-mcp is read-only as of 16 Sep 2026 (1.5k stars, last push 20 Aug, MIT) — PyPI elevenlabs-mcp 0.12.2 from 4 Aug 2026 still installs and still runs, so the stdio command above is not broken, but it is frozen and will not get new models. Two days before archiving it, on 14 Sep 2026, ElevenLabs extended the OAuth endpoint to ElevenCreative: speech, Scribe transcription across 99 languages, dubbing, music, sound effects, and 50+ image and video models, in Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor. Treat that as rolling out rather than finished, because the vendor contradicts itself — the hosted-MCP reference docs still describe agent management (create, duplicate, inspect, cost agents) plus a single text-to-speech tool, and elevenlabs.io/mcp still prints 'creative tools coming soon' three days after the announcement. Run tools/list against your own workspace before you plan a pipeline on it. The tools_sample above was verified against the local server, not the remote. Hosted output lands in an ElevenCreative workspace instead of coming back as local files, which is a real pipeline difference if you were shelling out to ffmpeg next. Regional endpoints exist (api.us, plus EU, India and Singapore variants) and workspace admins can restrict tool access and data residency. Credits are consumed by every tool either way. On the archived local path: ELEVENLABS_MCP_BASE_PATH (default ~/Desktop) is a hard security boundary for input files as well as output — any local path a tool reads must resolve inside it, so point it at your media root or reads will be rejected; other env is ELEVENLABS_MCP_OUTPUT_MODE (files/resources/both, default files) and ELEVENLABS_API_RESIDENCY (enterprise-only).

servers.name: EmpirioLabs AI MCP
servers.tagline: Remote hub over 180+ hosted models: video, image, speech, 3D, plus GPUs by the hour.
servers.description: EmpirioLabs' official remote MCP puts its inference platform behind one streamable-HTTP endpoint — generate_video against Kling O3, Wan 2.7, Seedance 2.0 Pro, Hunyuan Video 1.5, Pixverse V5.6 and SVI 2.0 Pro, stills from Qwen Image 2.0, Seedream 5.0 Lite, Hunyuan Image 3 and Nova Canvas, speech from GLM-TTS and Gemini TTS, music from Stable Audio 2.5, plus transcription, 3D generation and a compose_video recipe step. Useful to a filmmaker-agent as a cheap second source for open-weights video models and for the rarer surfaces most hubs skip: 3D assets and per-hour GPU instances in the same connection.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http empiriolabs https://mcp.empiriolabs.ai/mcp

auth.key_url: OAuth 2.1 browser sign-in for Claude and ChatGPT; scripts and editors can instead send an EmpirioLabs API key as an Authorization: Bearer header. Scopes are per-toolset (media, models, jobs, gpu, hosted_agents, …)

servers.notes: Listed one day after launch: the repo was created 14 Sep 2026, has 0 stars and no LICENSE file, and is a README pointing at the hosted endpoint rather than server code. The endpoint itself is real — it serves OAuth protected-resource metadata naming platform.empiriolabs.ai — and the docs are unusually complete for a new service, but treat this as unproven and check pricing yourself before committing a pipeline to it. Only 13 of the 78 tools are media generation; 39 are GPU-cloud and hosted-agent plumbing that a film pipeline will never call, so scope the connection down if your client supports it. Two operational traps: generation tools block for at most 50 seconds and then hand back a job_id you have to poll via get_job, and output URLs are signed and expire, so download anything you intend to keep. Read-only catalog, job and usage tools cost nothing. No free tier — pay-as-you-go prepaid credits (crypto top-ups accepted) or weekly allowance plans from $19.90/mo, and those allowances are trivial for film work: Lite grants 20 seconds of video and 7 images per week, Max 240 seconds. Model naming is self-reported by the platform; verify a slug with list_models rather than trusting a marketing page. For anything load-bearing, fal and replicate have the track record this does not yet.

servers.name: Epidemic Sound MCP Server
servers.tagline: Search a cleared music and SFX catalogue, then download stems, from the agent.
servers.description: Epidemic Sound's official MCP server (beta) puts the licensed catalogue behind sixteen tools: keyword and similarity search across music, a matching search over sound effects, track adaptation that recuts a song to a target duration, AI voiceover generation with stock and user-made voices, and download tools that return full tracks, stems, edits or WAV effects. SearchExternalReferences resolves a Spotify reference so the agent can find the nearest cleared equivalent, which is the temp-track problem most edits actually have. For an agent cutting to picture it is the alternative to generative score: real recordings, now trimmable to the length of the scene.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add -s user --transport http epidemic-sound https://www.epidemicsound.com/a/mcp-service/mcp --header 'Authorization: Bearer ${EPIDEMIC_SOUND_API_KEY}'

auth.key_url: https://www.epidemicsound.com/account/api-keys (signed-in account page; one key per person, not shareable). Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Cursor can use the OAuth flow instead

servers.notes: Hosted Streamable HTTP and still labelled beta. Re-checked 2 Oct 2026, and the docs changed underneath this entry: every tool was renamed to PascalCase (search_music is now SearchRecordings, and so on — update any saved prompts), the count went from twelve to sixteen with an EditRecording/PollEditRecordingJob/DownloadRecordingEdit trio that adapts a track to a target duration, and API keys are now self-serve from your account's API Keys page rather than gated behind a partnership agreement. Keys are personal, cannot be shared, and expire after a year. OAuth uses Dynamic Client Registration but is restricted to vetted clients — the docs name Claude (Desktop and Code) and Cursor and say Epidemic Sound will not add redirect URIs on request, so anything else needs a key. The MCP docs say nothing about licensing; rights follow your Epidemic Sound plan, not the API, so confirm the subscription covers commercial use before you deliver an ad. No published rate limits. Use it where cleared recordings beat generated score; for generative alternatives see the ElevenLabs, Mureka and Sonilo entries.

servers.name: fal MCP Server
servers.tagline: One hosted endpoint to search, run and chain 1,000+ image, video and audio models.
servers.description: fal's official stateless MCP server gives agents the entire fal platform through eleven tools: discover models, search docs, read schemas and pricing, run inference, submit and cancel async jobs, collect results and upload files. For filmmakers it is the broadest single gateway — Veo, Kling, LTX-2, Hailuo, FLUX, Ideogram, plus audio like Stable Audio 2.5, CassetteAI SFX and Beatoven — behind one connector.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http fal-ai https://mcp.fal.ai/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_FAL_KEY"

auth.key_url: fal.ai dashboard → API Keys (sent as Authorization: Bearer header, never stored server-side); ChatGPT and Codex connect by OAuth through the fal plugin instead

servers.notes: Hosted and fully stateless; the MCP itself is free, you pay standard fal per-run pricing, and there are no rate limits beyond your normal account concurrency. OAuth has finally shipped, but only for ChatGPT and Codex via the fal plugin (you pick which fal account it bills under 'Use for MCP' in account settings). The docs no longer mention Claude Desktop or claude.ai custom connectors at all, so for Claude the documented route is still Claude Code with the key in an Authorization header; Cursor and Windsurf work the same way. Eleven tools, unchanged since August. Arguably the best single 'everything' server for a generative film pipeline, and the practical MCP route to models with no first-party server (LTX-2, Stable Audio, CassetteAI, Beatoven).

servers.name: fcp-mcp
servers.tagline: Final Cut Pro MCP with FCPXML editing, live control, media QC and Compressor dispatch.
servers.description: fcp-mcp gives agents a broad Final Cut Pro bench: parse and rewrite FCPXML, run QC for flash frames and gaps, build rough cuts, control FCP through AppleScript, analyze media through ffprobe, and send jobs to Apple Compressor. It matters when a filmmaker lives in Final Cut but still wants agent-operated timeline repair, captions, cross-NLE handoff, and export automation.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add-json fcp '{"type":"stdio","command":"fcp-mcp"}' --scope user

auth.key_url: Requires macOS 15.6+ with Final Cut Pro for live-control tools; FCPXML tools work without FCP, Python 3.10+ and FFmpeg on PATH are required for media tools, and Apple Compressor is optional

servers.notes: Name collision warning: this is dreliq9's Python server, PyPI package `fcp-mcp`. The `fcpxml-mcp` entry in this directory is DareDev256/fcp-mcp-server — a different maintainer with a nearly identical name. MIT. The release drift has not been fixed and has widened: PyPI is still on 0.2.0 from Apr 23 2026 — also the only git tag — while `main` (pushed Aug 13 2026) now documents a v0.3.0 with 94 tools across 13 categories. `pipx install fcp-mcp` therefore gets you the April build, not the README; install from git if you want what the README describes. Tool count is also profile-gated: FCP_MCP_PROFILE picks inspect/workflow/edit/full and defaults to `workflow`, so a fresh connection does not expose everything. Maturity caveat: 6 GitHub stars. Live control depends on AppleScript, a running Final Cut Pro and FCP_MCP_ENABLE_LIVE_CONTROL; optional FCP_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR changes where modified FCPXML is written and FCP_MCP_ALLOWED_ROOTS widens the readable paths.

servers.name: FCPXML MCP
servers.tagline: Turn Final Cut Pro XML into QC, markers, rough cuts, and cross-NLE handoffs.
servers.description: FCPXML MCP gives agents a deep Final Cut Pro XML workbench: inspect timelines, detect flash frames and gaps, add marker batches, build rough cuts, reformat cuts, export EDL/CSV, and write Resolve or FCP7 handoff files. It fits the assistant-editor jobs that do not require eyes on the frame: count, QC, annotate, restructure, and push a clean XML back into the edit bay.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add fcpxml -e FCP_PROJECTS_DIR=~/Movies -- uvx fcp-mcp-server

auth.key_url: XML mode works on exported FCPXML files; Live Mode requires macOS with Final Cut Pro 10.4+ running and a one-time Automation permission grant

servers.notes: Rename direction, corrected — an earlier version of this note had it backwards. `DareDev256/fcpxml-mcp-server` is the OLD path and 301-redirects to the canonical `DareDev256/fcp-mcp-server`; use the latter. Name collision warning: the `fcp-mcp` entry in this directory is dreliq9's separate Final Cut server, not this one. MIT, v0.16.0 tagged Aug 16 2026 and on PyPI Aug 19, 95 stars, Python >=3.10, PyPI `fcp-mcp-server`, MCP SDK 1.3 through 2.x, Final Cut Pro 10.4–12.x. Since v0.14.0 the advertised surface is 7 grouped tools (inspect/diagnose/edit/mark/generate/transcript/deliver) dispatching 62 underlying operations; set FCP_MCP_LEGACY_TOOLS=1 to advertise the old flat tool names. Read the sandbox docs before pointing it at a shared machine: FCP_PROJECTS_DIR confines *listing* only and never restricts which files a tool can open — the opt-in FCP_PROJECTS_DIRS (PATH-separated roots, new in 0.16.0) is the variable that actually confines reads, and it is off by default. This is not an in-FCP plugin: Live Mode pushes XML into Final Cut via an Apple event, but current timelines still come back by manual File > Export XML.

servers.name: FFmpeg MCP
servers.tagline: Conversational FFmpeg: trim, concat, overlay, scale, and extract frames locally.
servers.description: Wraps the FFmpeg CLI as MCP tools for finding, probing, cutting, merging, compositing, and resizing local video files. A thin, readable surface for agent-side post on generated clips — no cloud upload, no credits — but it has been quiet since May 2026 and Kinocut now covers the same ground with more care.

install.stdio_command: uv --directory /path/to/ffmpeg-mcp run ffmpeg-mcp (after cloning the repo)

servers.notes: 144 stars, still pushed May 20 2026 — over three months quiet, and the last commit was a security fix (shlex-quoting paths against FFmpeg argument injection, CWE-88), so treat that as the floor of its hardening rather than a maintained baseline. Caveats: README states macOS only (ARM64 or x86_64), and install means cloning the repo and running `uv sync` — there is no published package, so the stdio command needs your own checkout path. The older egoist/ffmpeg-mcp has been dormant since Mar 2025. Alternatives: kevinwatt/ffmpeg-mcp-lite (26 stars, last pushed May 8 2026 — no more current than this one) and Kinocut (listed here under the mcp-video slug), which is cross-platform, actively released, and adds guardrails on top of FFmpeg. On current evidence Kinocut is the better default and this entry is the minimal-surface fallback.

servers.name: FilmLab
servers.tagline: Hosted film lab: storyboard, generate, review, and export, with the price shown before each run.
servers.description: FilmLab is the generative workbench attached to TheFilmRadar, a German-language industry platform for DACH film and TV crews, and it exposes its whole ten-stage pipeline over one OAuth-gated remote MCP. Thirty-seven tools cover project and pipeline context, auto-storyboarding, image and clip generation in batches, a review queue with contact sheets and continuity checks, a full location board that can generate variants and panoramas from a reference image, and sequence assembly through to export profiles and render jobs. The two things that distinguish it from the rest of the studio tier are the review stage — assets get a verdict before they reach a sequence — and cost preflight, which quotes credits before a run rather than after. Reading, browsing, and project creation cost nothing, so an agent can survey a project before anything is spent.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http filmlab https://mcp-lab.thefilmradar.com/mcp

auth.key_url: OAuth against a FilmRadar account at https://lab.thefilmradar.com — no API key and no token to paste

servers.notes: New and unproven: published to the official MCP registry on 2026-08-17 as com.thefilmradar/filmlab, with three versions shipped that same day and 1.1.1 still current as of 2026-10-01 — no registry release since. Endpoint re-checked 2026-10-01: https://mcp-lab.thefilmradar.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource returns resource metadata naming itself the authorization server, header bearer only. The vendor docs now list 37 tools in six groups (up from 34 in August), including location management — create, delete, restyle, panorama, image analysis — and lab_delete_location is a destructive tool, so scope your agent's permissions accordingly. Tool names come from those docs, not from a tools/list this directory could read, because there is no anonymous access. Closed source, no repo, one operator, and the docs and UI are German-first — the MCP page is entirely in German, which is friction if your agent or your crew is not. It also does not name the models behind lab_generate and lab_animate ('Soul Cinema' is a house label, not an engine), so you are buying credits without knowing which engine renders them; Martini and Nomi both publish their model rosters. Billing is per run with the price quoted first: reads, browsing, previews and project creation are free, while generation, animation, locations and exports draw on credits bought in the Composer. Correction to earlier notes here: the MCP page now states credits are valid for three months (AGB § 7), so do not stockpile them.

servers.name: Fish Audio MCP
servers.tagline: Hosted Fish Audio server: voice search, expressive TTS, transcription, plus image and video generation.
servers.description: Fish Audio's official hosted MCP server connects an agent to your Fish Audio account over OAuth: browse and search the voice library, generate speech steered with inline tags like [whispering] or [excited], transcribe local or uploaded audio, and — since mid-September 2026 — generate and edit images and run text-to-video and image-to-video. For a filmmaker-agent the draw is temp dialogue and scratch VO with emotional direction written into the script line, plus transcripts for the edit, from one connection billed against the plan you already have.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http fish-audio https://api.fish.audio/mcp

auth.key_url: Browser OAuth with your Fish Audio account; you pick the team the connection works in

servers.notes: Hosted only and closed source — no npm or PyPI package, no public server repo. The endpoint answers 405 to a GET on 26 Sep 2026, consistent with a POST-only streamable HTTP server. The docs describe capabilities but publish no tool list, so tools_sample is null rather than guessed; the docs PR that added image and video (merged 17 Sep 2026) names only t2i, edit, t2v and i2v variants and deliberately leaves lip-sync out of the MCP. Billing draws from your plan's package credits, not developer API credits, and image or video jobs are quoted first and wait for your confirmation. Video needs Plus ($11/mo promo, $15 list) or higher; the free tier gets a daily image allowance and is personal, non-commercial use only, so anything headed for a paying client needs a paid plan. Connections are scoped to one team. Local files sent for transcription are uploaded to a temporary slot deleted after 7 days; generated outputs come back as permanent URLs, so assume anything you generate is reachable by link. Do not confuse it with Fish Audio's separate read-only docs MCP at docs.fish.audio/mcp, or with the community wrappers (da-okazaki/mcp-fish-audio-server, AceDataCloud/FishMCP), which are not maintained by Fish Audio.

servers.name: FLUX MCP
servers.tagline: Official BFL server: FLUX.2 stills and editing, now with FLUX 3 video generation.
servers.description: Black Forest Labs' official hosted MCP exposes the FLUX.2 toolkit — generation, image editing, multi-reference composition, variations and history — with automatic routing to the right model (Klein for sub-second drafts up to Max for production assets). It now also drives FLUX 3 video: text-to-video, keyframe animation and clip continuation, plus a full-quality re-render of a draft that preserves composition and seed. For filmmakers it is a top-tier stills, concept-art and frame-editing engine that can carry a chosen frame straight into motion.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http flux https://mcp.bfl.ai

auth.key_url: OAuth-only: sign in with your BFL account and pick a billing org; tokens auto-refresh

servers.notes: Re-checked 8 Oct 2026 with no drift in the core: endpoint, OAuth-only auth and all seven tools still match the docs, and the repo (MIT, not archived) was last pushed 29 Sep 2026. Image models: flux2_pro_preview (default), flux2_max, flux2_klein_9b_preview, flux2_klein_4b, flux2_flex (typography); vto is its own tool, not a model value, and passing it as one fails. generate_image batches 1-8 images in parallel. Video runs on flux3_video in t2v, i2v and v2v modes, up to 4 clips per call, 5-20 s or auto, hd or fhd, with audio on by default. generate_video returns a pending request_id and clips take minutes — fetch them with get_result, which the docs now mention alongside a bfl://models catalog resource. Render with draft: true first (cheaper, hd only) to check motion and timing, then enhance_video re-renders the same draft at full quality. BFL also publishes optional Claude Code skills (flux-image-best-practices, flux-3-video) via the black-forest-labs/skills plugin marketplace. Listed under image generation because that is still the bulk of the surface. Pricing at bfl.ai/pricing.

servers.name: Frame.io MCP
servers.tagline: Adobe's hosted Frame.io MCP: review comments, shares, version stacks, uploads, and metadata.
servers.description: Frame.io's official remote MCP server puts the review-and-approval layer of a production in front of an agent: search assets across workspaces, read and write review comments, build version stacks, upload media, edit metadata fields, and manage share links, reviewers, and project members. Adobe says it adds nothing the V4 API cannot already do. What it adds is the ability to chain those calls from a prompt. For a film pipeline, that means turning a round of client notes into a task list, or stacking the new cut on the old one and sending the share link, without anyone opening the browser.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http frameio https://mcp.frame.io/v1/mcp

auth.key_url: OAuth through Adobe IMS — sign in with the Adobe ID linked to your Frame.io account

servers.notes: Public beta as of 7 Oct 2026, per Adobe staff on the forum thread that announced a private beta on 29 Jul. Self-serve now, with no onboarding call, but expect beta churn. Anyone who configured it before 7 Oct should check they are on the /v1/mcp URL. Frame.io Legacy accounts are not supported at all. Adobe Managed Accounts can land in the wrong organization if a stale Adobe session is reused; the docs give a fix. Tools run with your own permissions, so uploads need Contributor access. The write surface is real: `delete_resources` permanently deletes everything except files and folders, which `restore_assets` can bring back. Adobe recommends approving each write or delete call, which is the correct default in front of a client's review project. Adobe's docs give click-through steps for Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code and Copilot CLI, but not a Claude Code command. The command above is the standard remote-HTTP form against the documented URL, and the endpoint's OAuth discovery document answers (checked 10 Oct 2026). There is no source repo, and the docs do not cover MCP-specific pricing; usage counts against your Frame.io plan. Supersedes the community `frameio` entry for every account except Legacy ones.

servers.name: Frame.io MCP (community)
servers.tagline: 74 tools over the Frame.io V4 API — comments, shares, version stacks, uploads.
servers.description: A local stdio MCP server for the Frame.io v4 API, built on FastMCP over Adobe's official Python SDK: browse workspaces and projects, upload and download footage, leave timecode-accurate review comments, create client share links, manage version stacks, apply custom metadata in bulk, and manage webhooks. Adobe now runs its own hosted server, listed as `frameio-official`, so this one matters mainly as a self-hosted, self-credentialed alternative.

install.stdio_command: uvx frameio-mcp serve (after a one-time uvx frameio-mcp login --client-id YOUR_ADOBE_SPA_CLIENT_ID)

auth.key_url: https://developer.adobe.com/console — add the Frame.io API and an OAuth Single Page App credential with redirect URI https://localhost:8723/callback; tokens land in ~/.frameio-mcp/tokens.json

servers.notes: The Claude Code plugin route is dead. github.com/bowlofarugula/frameio-plugins still 404s (rechecked 2026-09-30), so the old '/plugin marketplace add' command cannot work and claude_code is null. PyPI frameio-mcp 0.1.0 (uploaded 2026-06-04, not yanked) is still the only release. A uvx frameio-mcp --help and status run on 2026-08-11 installed clean. It needs Python 3.13+, and you must register your own Adobe OAuth SPA credential before it does anything. Its stated source repo has since been rewritten into a remote Cloudflare Workers server that you would have to deploy yourself. That repo still has 0 stars and has not been pushed since 2026-06-13, and its /authorize fails closed behind a redirect-URI allowlist, so there is no public endpoint. This is effectively unmaintained: treat it as a working snapshot, not a project. Use `frameio-official` instead unless you are on a Frame.io Legacy account. Adobe's own server went to public beta on 2026-10-07 with a documented hosted endpoint and Adobe ID OAuth, which removes the reason this entry existed. Legacy accounts are the one gap left: the official server does not support them. This server is built on the v4 API, so it has not been shown to work for them either.

servers.name: Framesail
servers.tagline: Hosted MCP that carries a script through storyboard, voiceover and shots to a cut MP4.
servers.description: Framesail's own remote MCP exposes its six-stage pipeline to an agent: derive a look from reference images, video or a YouTube link, write or generate the script, lock reference images for every character, place and prop, record voiceover with word-level timing, plan the storyboard scene by scene, then render each shot against those locked references and export with captions, music and SFX. State lives server-side, so a run can pause between chat sessions and resume, and an agent can read or rewrite the script, references and storyboard before the next stage runs. Aimed at long-form output rather than clips, which makes it one of the few studio-class servers an agent can drive end to end.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http framesail https://api.framesail.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer fsk_YOUR_KEY"

auth.key_url: https://framesail.com/developers — Claude Code and Cursor use an fsk_ bearer token; claude.ai, Claude Desktop and the mobile app connect over OAuth instead and need no key.

servers.notes: Verified 18 Sep 2026 from the vendor's own pages: the endpoint, transport, both auth paths and the connect command come from framesail.com/developers, and an anonymous GET on api.framesail.com/mcp answers 401, so the server is live and gated. Price is the first thing to check, because there is no free tier and MCP is not on the entry plan: quarterly billing runs Creator $22/month (12,000 credits), Pro $54/month (30,000), Studio $137/month (80,000) and Scale $551/month (330,000), and 'API & MCP access' is listed from Pro upward. Credits roll over but expire two months after they are granted, so a quiet month is a forfeited month. Only three tool names are published — generate_script, generate_storyboard and export_video — so tools_sample lists those three rather than a number; third-party directories quote a tool count the vendor does not, and we did not run tools/list without a paid key. Hosted only: no repo, no local package, nothing to self-host, and no way to audit what the pipeline sends to which upstream model. The vendor also ships a REST API over the same stages and says to pick one surface per run rather than mixing MCP and REST. If you want the same script-to-cut arc with a timeline you can actually edit, compare martini; if you only need the breakdown and prompts and will generate elsewhere, penshot does that part for free.

servers.name: FrameThrower
servers.tagline: Cinematography reference: search film stills from 5,489 films by lighting, lens, shot size, colour and mood.
servers.description: A remote MCP server over one of the largest film still libraries on the internet — 5,489 films indexed frame by frame on lighting key and quality, lens character, shot size, camera angle, colour palette in hex, mood and era. An agent searches in plain language, narrows by craft attribute, and refines from any frame the user reacts to, which is the loop a director or DP actually works in when building a lookbook or shot list. Returns metadata, thumbnails, colour palettes and deep links — never raw image bytes, so it is a reference tool rather than a source of generation inputs.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http framethrower https://framethrower.ai/api/mcp

auth.key_url: OAuth 2.1 — the client opens a FrameThrower sign-in; the agent then acts as that account. No API key.

servers.notes: Endpoint, four tools, OAuth 2.1, credit pricing and the 5,489-film index all unchanged on re-check. Remote and hosted, so nothing to install or keep running. Free tier is $2 of credits on signup with no card; each tool call costs 2 credits at $1 = 1,000 credits, so $1 covers 500 calls, and credits do not expire; top-ups come in $20 packs. No rate limits — when credits run out the tool returns the balance rather than failing silently. Frames are shown at reduced resolution as references for commentary and study — rights remain with their owners, and the server never returns image bytes. One-vendor operation: the repo (framethrower-ai/framethrower-mcp) is a README pointing at the hosted endpoint and has not been touched since 12 Aug 2026, so there is no code to audit and no second maintainer if the service lapses. Submitted by the vendor.

servers.name: Freepik MCP

Kept listed so old links and configs resolve to an explanation rather than a blank page.

Re-checked 8 Oct 2026: the repo still 404s to both the GitHub API and an anonymous fetch, and it was not renamed inside the org; freepik-company still exists, its only MCP repos are the unrelated prometheus-mcp and jev-mcp (a typed-decision server, nothing to do with images), and it now carries a homebrew-magnific tap. Freepik rebranded to Magnific in April 2026 and the developer platform followed — docs.freepik.com still 301s to docs.magnific.com, whose llms.txt lists Mystic, upscalers, video, audio and stock endpoints against api.magnific.com with no Freepik references left. servers.name: Freesound MCP Server
servers.tagline: Search freesound.org's CC-licensed sound library by natural language for SFX pulls.

For a film pipeline this covers the classic library-pull workflow ('thunder for a storm scene, under 30s') with the license metadata attached, complementing generative SFX tools.

install.stdio_command: Clone the repo, then `docker build -t freesound-mcp .` or run from source with uv — no published package

auth.key_url: https://freesound.org/apiv2/apply/ (login required)

servers.notes: MIT, ~7 stars, last pushed 24 Jun 2025 and still untouched on 26 Sep 2026 — listed because it is the tidiest option for a library nothing else covers, not because anyone is maintaining it. Search-only: it returns preview URLs, not downloads, so a separate fetch step is still on you. The README's API-key link (freesound.org/api/apply/) 404s; the working one is freesound.org/apiv2/apply/, which bounces you through a Freesound login first. No PyPI release: clone and build. The alternatives are no healthier — MuShan-bit/freesound-mcp adds download by sound ID (1 star, Jan 2026) and timjrobinson/FreesoundMCPServer is Node.js (2 stars, Jul 2025). Freesound licences are per-sound and include CC-BY and non-commercial terms — read each one before it goes in a film.

servers.name: Getty Images MCP Server
servers.tagline: Official remote MCP for searching and downloading licensed Getty stills and footage.
servers.description: Getty Images' hosted MCP server, launched 12 Aug 2026, exposes the creative, editorial, news, sport, and archival library to agents: search stills and video, read asset metadata, and download files under your organization's existing licence. For a film team it is the licensed-archive counterpart to generative video — the route an agent takes when a cut needs real news footage, sports plates, or historical material that no model can lawfully fabricate. Tools are meant to be discovered at runtime rather than hard-coded.

auth.key_url: API key and secret from your Getty Images account representative — https://engage.gettyimages.com/MCP-contact-sales

servers.notes: Enterprise-gated, not self-serve: access needs an active Getty agreement (Premium Access or Editorial Subscription) or a reseller partnership, acceptance of the Web Service Terms, and an API key plus secret issued by an account rep — there is no signup link, only contact-sales. Re-checked 17 Sep 2026 and nothing has moved in five weeks: same endpoint, same 20-queries-per-second throttle, same OAuth 2.0 client-credentials or authorization-code handshake, and still no published header form, client config snippet, or tool names. So claude_code stays null until the connect recipe is public; point your agent at the server and let it read the auth and tool descriptions there. Getty asks explicitly that you not hard-code tool names or parameters, because they are still changing. The sharp edge is licensing, not plumbing: search spans the whole library while downloads are bounded by your subscription, so an agent can surface an asset it has no right to deliver — check the licence before you cut it in. Nothing here generates; for a self-serve licensed-footage route see stockfilm, and for stills-with-an-open-API see magnific.

servers.name: Google Drive MCP
servers.tagline: Google's official remote Drive MCP: search, read, and create files with Workspace governance.
servers.description: A first-party hosted MCP endpoint from the Drive API team that lets agents search files, read content as a natural-language representation, retrieve metadata, and create/download files — inheriting the user's Drive permissions and Workspace data governance. The production file server for dailies, exports, and shared media.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http google-drive https://drivemcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1

auth.key_url: Bring your own Google Cloud OAuth client (consent screen + client ID/secret) — see the configure-mcp-server guide

servers.notes: Still gated behind the Google Workspace Developer Preview Program more than three months after listing, with no GA announcement — flag as preview. Nothing drifted on re-check: same endpoint, same eight tools, same two scopes (drive.readonly and drive.file, not full Drive access). Google has since published a per-tool MCP reference at developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/reference/mcp, which is the place to check argument shapes. The setup cost is the same as before and worth budgeting for: enable both the Drive API and the Drive MCP API in your own Google Cloud project, configure the consent screen, then create a Web application OAuth client whose redirect URI depends on the client you are connecting from — Google documents different values for Antigravity, Claude and everything else, and a mismatch fails at consent, not at connect. The old Anthropic reference gdrive server is archived; don't use it. Broader community alternative covering Docs/Sheets/Slides/Gmail too: taylorwilsdon/google_workspace_mcp, listed here as google-workspace.

servers.name: Google GenMedia MCP
servers.tagline: Google Cloud's MCP servers for Veo, Gemini Omni, Lyria, Chirp TTS and ffmpeg compositing.
servers.description: A suite of Go-based MCP servers from Google Cloud's GenMedia Creative Studio repo: Veo text/image-to-video plus extension and first/last-frame tools, a Gemini Omni video server, Nano Banana and Gemini stills, Lyria music, Chirp 3 TTS, and an AVTool server wrapping ffmpeg for compositing. The closest thing to an official Veo MCP, and a full agentic production toolchain on Vertex AI.

install.stdio_command: One binary per model. Install them all with the repo's script — curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/vertex-ai-creative-studio/main/experiments/mcp-genmedia/mcp-genmedia-go/install-online.sh | bash — or build from source with go work sync && go install ./mcp-avtool-go ./mcp-chirp3-go ./mcp-gemini-go ./mcp-nanobanana-go ./mcp-imagen-go ./mcp-lyria-go ./mcp-veo-go, adding ./mcp-omni-go which the README's line still omits, then point your client at each binary (mcp-veo-go for Veo) with GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT set

auth.key_url: Google Cloud project with Vertex AI enabled; uses Application Default Credentials (gcloud auth application-default login)

servers.notes: Official Google Cloud code but explicitly experimental (lives in /experiments). Busier than ever — 1,202 stars, pushed 2026-09-05, VERSION 3.18.1 cut 2026-08-29. Now eight servers, not seven: mcp-omni-go landed alongside mcp-gemini-go, wrapping gemini-omni-1.1-flash-preview through the Vertex Interactions API. Veo has grown veo_extend_video, veo_first_last_to_video and veo_reference_to_video and defaults to veo-3.1-fast-generate-001; Lyria is on lyria-3-clip-preview. Imagen is the casualty: install.sh now skips mcp-imagen-go outright, with the comment 'Imagen deprecation as of June 30, 2026', so treat imagen_t2i as on its way out and use mcp-nanobanana-go for stills. Install is still the rough edge — no npx one-liner, no published claude mcp add, so you pipe install-online.sh to bash or go install per directory and wire each binary in yourself; the README's go install line has not caught up with mcp-omni-go. Omni is preview-gated and calls the global-only Interactions endpoint, ignoring regional overrides. Supports stdio/HTTP/SSE and GCS or local output; ships agent skills for storyboarding. With Sora leaving the API on 2026-09-24, this is the most direct official route to Veo 3.1 for an agent.

servers.name: Google Workspace MCP
servers.tagline: Full Google Workspace control — Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Gmail, Calendar and more.
servers.description: The most comprehensive community Workspace MCP: 120+ tools across 12 Google services, with OAuth 2.0/2.1 multi-user support and tool tiers. For film teams: Drive media file search/read/share plus Docs (scripts), Sheets (budgets and shot lists), Slides (pitch decks), Gmail, and Calendar — one server for the whole production office.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add google-workspace -e GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=YOUR_ID -e GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=YOUR_SECRET -- uvx workspace-mcp --tool-tier core

auth.key_url: OAuth client from Google Cloud Console (https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials)

servers.notes: 3.2k stars, MIT, still shipping fast — v1.26.2 landed 15 Sep 2026 and the env vars and uvx command above are unchanged. What did change is the recommended transport: the README now files stdio under 'legacy configuration ... for clients without Connector support' and prescribes HTTP everywhere else, including Claude Code, where the documented path is to start the server in HTTP mode and run `claude mcp add --transport http workspace-mcp http://localhost:8000/mcp`. The stdio one-liner above still works and still needs no long-running process, which is why it stays; take the HTTP route if you want OAuth 2.1 multi-user, read-only enforcement across users, or Connector support in Claude web, desktop and mobile. Tool tiers keep the context small (--tool-tier core; extended and complete exist), and --tools, --disabled-tools and --read-only trim it further. You still supply your own Google Cloud OAuth client, which is the real setup cost: about five minutes of console work per deployment. The repo now also ships a bundled Claude skill (skills/managing-google-workspace) to keep an agent from flailing across 120+ tools. Documentation lives at workspacemcp.com, where the maintainer also sells a managed cloud instance — the self-hosted server remains free and MIT. npx-only Drive-focused alternative: piotr-agier/google-drive-mcp (219 stars, pushed 16 Sep 2026).

servers.name: Griptape Nodes
servers.tagline: Foundry's node-based AI workflow engine, drivable by an outside agent over local HTTP.
servers.description: Griptape Nodes is a drag-and-drop generative-AI workflow builder from Foundry — the Nuke company — with libraries covering Google Veo and Imagen, FLUX, Luma, Topaz, ElevenLabs, WAN and LTX, plus first-party bridges out to Nuke, Blender and USD. The engine you run locally exposes its own Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint, so an external agent can drive the graph rather than only operating inside Griptape's editor. For a filmmaker that makes it the rare hub where the model roster and the compositing app share one orchestration layer.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http griptape-nodes http://localhost:8125/mcp/
install.stdio_command: uv tool install griptape-nodes (shorthand `gtn`), or the managed Griptape Nodes Desktop app for macOS/Windows/Linux; the engine must be running before a client can connect

auth.key_url: https://nodes.griptape.ai — sign in to generate the Griptape API key the engine needs; the MCP endpoint itself has no auth

servers.notes: Read the licence before you bill a client: Foundry's pricing page puts the free tier under 'Non-Commercial', single user, testing only. Professional is $40/user/month (or $400/year, capped at three users) and includes $40 of model credits — running open-source models locally or wiring in your own provider keys does not spend them. The engine is closed source, so links.repo is null: PyPI griptape-nodes is proprietary-licensed (0.99.0, published 22 Sep 2026, after four minor releases in a month — the cadence is real), and github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-app 404s to the public. The node libraries are open, Apache-2.0, and moving: griptape-nodes-library-nuke was last pushed 25 Sep 2026. Two things to know about the MCP endpoint — it binds to localhost:8125 with no authentication at all (Griptape's own docs warn you not to bind 0.0.0.0), and the tool surface is not published anywhere, so run tools/list once connected; tools_sample stays null rather than guessed. Override the bind with GTN_MCP_SERVER_HOST and GTN_MCP_SERVER_PORT. Foundry acquired Griptape on 18 Feb 2026 and the deeper Nuke agent work shown at NAB is still early access, so this endpoint is what you can actually connect to today.

servers.name: Hedra MCP (Official)
servers.tagline: Hedra's own hosted MCP: one OAuth URL onto its whole image, video and audio catalogue.
servers.description: Hedra shipped a first-party remote MCP alongside its CLI on 2026-08-31, which quietly turns a talking-avatar vendor into an inference hub an agent can address directly. One endpoint reaches the platform roster — Veo 3.1, Sora 2 Pro, Kling 2.6 Pro, Seedance 2.5, Hailuo 2.3, Luma Ray 3.2 and Hedra's own Character 3 for video; Nano Banana Pro, GPT Image 2, Seedream 4.5 and Flux.2 [max] for stills; ElevenLabs voice, music and SFX for sound. Hedra also advertises visual understanding on the same connection, so a filmmaker-agent can look at the frame it just rendered before deciding the next shot.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http hedra https://mcp.hedra.com

auth.key_url: Browser OAuth against https://auth.hedra.com — S256 PKCE with an open registration_endpoint, so there is no key to paste. The separate CLI takes HEDRA_API_KEY from https://www.hedra.com/develop/api-keys.

servers.notes: Verified 2026-09-09 from Hedra's own pages. The connect line above is copied verbatim from hedra.com/mcp, and the OAuth chain checks out: mcp.hedra.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource names https://auth.hedra.com as the authorization server with bearer-header auth, and that server publishes authorization_code, refresh_token and device_code grants, S256 PKCE and a registration_endpoint, so Dynamic Client Registration works and no pre-shared credential is needed. Two caveats. First, the only scopes advertised are openid, profile, email and offline_access — nothing generation-specific — so the token is an identity token and your reach is whatever your Hedra account can already do, with no way to hand an agent a narrower grant. Second, no tool list is published anywhere: the setup page gives a URL and nothing else, the server is closed source with no repo, and hedra-labs' public repos cover only the CLI and SDKs. Call tools/list and find out. Billing is 'your Hedra subscription or pay as you go' against the same credits as the app, and the roster is Hedra's to churn — Sora 2 is listed today but leaves OpenAI's API on 2026-09-24. For named Character-3 tools driven by a plain API key instead of OAuth, the community `hedra` server still does that and this one does not document it.

servers.name: Hedra MCP Server
servers.tagline: Character-3 talking-avatar video, TTS, and image generation through Hedra's API.
servers.description: Node MCP server for Hedra's generation API: lip-synced character video from an image plus audio (Character-3), text-to-speech, image generation, and asset/credit management. Its README also advertises third-party models reachable through Hedra Studio, though that list dates from the server's only release and has since drifted from Hedra's own roster.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add hedra -e HEDRA_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY -- npx -y mcp-server-hedra

auth.key_url: https://www.hedra.com/develop/api-keys (requires a paid Hedra subscription)

servers.notes: No longer the only way in: Hedra shipped an official hosted MCP on 2026-08-31 at mcp.hedra.com, listed here as `hedra-official`, and it is the better default — OAuth instead of a pasted key, and the current model roster instead of a frozen one. Reach for this community server only when you want named Character-3 tools driven by a plain API key, which the official endpoint does not document. Re-checked 2026-09-09 and nothing here has moved: npm mcp-server-hedra is still the 1.0.0 published 2026-02-08, the repo has had no push since the same day, MIT, Node 18+, 2 stars. Drifts to expect against its README: the key page is hedra.com/develop/api-keys (the README's /api-profile link is stale), and the third-party model list has aged badly — Hedra's platform now fronts Seedance 2.5, MiniMax Hailuo 2.3, Kling 2.6 Pro and Nano Banana Pro, while Sora 2 leaves OpenAI's API on 2026-09-24. Character-3 itself is alive and still on Hedra's model page. The API bills against the same Studio credit balance as the app and needs a paid subscription.

servers.name: HeyGen Remote MCP
servers.tagline: Hosted MCP for avatar videos, lipsync, and 175-language video translation.
