The published tool surface spans Video Agent one-prompt and multi-turn generation, video translation with lip-sync (175+ languages), lipsync jobs, avatar groups and looks, templates, voice design and cloning, music and SFX search, AI clipping of long footage, filler-word removal, brand kits and glossaries, and batches of up to 100 videos, translations, or lipsyncs per request.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http heygen https://mcp.heygen.com/mcp/v1/

auth.key_url: One-time browser OAuth tied to your HeyGen account

servers.notes: Endpoint, OAuth flow and plan terms re-confirmed against HeyGen's own MCP docs on 2026-09-08: unchanged, available on all HeyGen plans, generation consumes plan credits, no API key. There is still no local option: HeyGen's own heygen-com/heygen-mcp 404s, and the community fork this entry used to recommend (sbroenne/heygen-mcp) has 404'd too — its PyPI package heygen-mcp-sbroenne is still installable but frozen at 0.3.1 from 2026-01-31 with its source gone, so treat it as abandoned. The hosted remote is the only maintained route. HeyGen's official Agent Skills (heygen-com/skills) remain active — 429 stars, still pushed 2026-07-14, so the skills repo has gained attention but no commits in nearly two months.

servers.name: Higgsfield MCP
servers.tagline: Hosted connector to 30+ models: Seedance 2.5, Kling 3, Soul 2.0, Nano Banana Pro.
servers.description: Higgsfield's official hosted MCP exposes its platform — advertised as 30+ models — through one OAuth endpoint. The models named on its own MCP page as of September 2026 are Seedance 2.5, Seedance 2.0, Kling 3, Soul 2.0, Nano Banana Pro, Google Omni Flash, Seedream 5.0 Lite and GPT Image 2, with Cinema Studio, Flux, MiniMax Hailuo and Veo listed in the wider roster. Agents can generate 4K images, videos up to 15s, train consistent characters and browse creation history on existing Higgsfield plan credits.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http higgsfield https://mcp.higgsfield.ai/mcp

auth.key_url: Sign in with your Higgsfield account during connector setup — no API keys

servers.notes: Re-checked 5 Sep 2026: endpoint still answers 401 unauthenticated, so it is alive and OAuth-gated, and the published roster is unchanged. Sora is no longer in the roster — OpenAI is retiring it, so do not plan around it here. tools_sample stays null because the endpoint requires auth and Higgsfield publishes no tool list; call tools/list after connecting. Works with Claude and any MCP client; also ships a CLI and agent skills.

servers.name: Houdini MCP
servers.tagline: Drive SideFX Houdini nodes and procedural FX from your agent.
servers.description: Two credible community servers cover Houdini. capoomgit/houdini-mcp is the original: a Python plugin plus bridge script that creates and wires nodes and executes code over a localhost socket. healkeiser/fxhoudinimcp is the larger and more actively developed one — 188 tools across SOPs, LOPs/USD, DOPs, PDG/TOPs, COPs, HDAs, animation, rendering and VEX, with a one-command installer. Either opens Houdini's procedural FX and sim toolset to agent-driven work; neither is from SideFX.

install.stdio_command: pip install fxhoudinimcp && python -m fxhoudinimcp install (registers both the Houdini package and the client entry). capoomgit/houdini-mcp is manual: copy its plugin into the Houdini scripts dir.

auth.key_url: Requires Houdini running with the plugin installed — fxhoudinimcp needs Houdini 20.5+ and a Python 3.10+ outside Houdini; capoomgit/houdini-mcp listens on localhost:9876

servers.notes: healkeiser/fxhoudinimcp: 190 stars, MIT, PyPI 2.10.0 (Jul 29 2026), tested through Houdini 22.0.368 — fewer stars than the original but far broader coverage and the better-maintained of the two; it is the one to try first. capoomgit/houdini-mcp: 285 stars, MIT, last push Jun 11 2026, still early-stage and manual to install. SideFX itself has no shipping MCP: the H22 'APEX Script comfort package' (AI-assisted rigging-code authoring, autocomplete, validation) was shown at the Houdini 22 keynote and SideFX's own page calls it 'a preview for a tool which will be released later on' — trade coverage from SIGGRAPH 2026 describes an APEX Script MCP server headed to SideFX Labs, but as of Sep 2026 SideFX has not documented one and it is not in the core product. Do not plan a pipeline around it yet. For Cinema 4D, Maxon now ships an official server inside C4D 2026.4 (see cinema4d); on older versions the community ttiimmaacc/cinema4d-mcp (129 stars, last push Mar 2026, C4D 2024+, MoGraph/Redshift tools) is the equivalent.

servers.name: Hume MCP Server
servers.tagline: Official Hume server for Octave TTS — emotionally expressive, acting-directed speech.
servers.description: Hume's official MCP server drives Octave, a speech-language model that performs text rather than merely pronouncing it, with prompt-directed emotion and delivery. Ideal for film dialogue and narration where acting nuance matters; agents can iterate on takes, save designed voices to a library, and replay prior audio without regenerating.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add hume -e HUME_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY -- npx @humeai/mcp-server

auth.key_url: https://platform.hume.ai

servers.notes: Official but effectively dormant, and the gap keeps widening: npm @humeai/mcp-server is still 0.3.0, published 8 Jan 2026 — over eight months with no release. The GitHub repo reports a push on 26 Aug 2026, but that is not the default branch: the newest commit on main is still 'bump v (#17)' from 8 Jan 2026, so read the push date as branch noise, not maintenance. ~9 stars, 3 open issues, no LICENSE file in the tree even though npm metadata declares ISC. Hume's docs site also serves a separate MCP at https://dev.hume.ai/_mcp/server, but that is Mintlify documentation search (one searchDocs tool) — it will not synthesize a line of dialogue, so do not wire it in expecting Octave. Five tools — a much narrower surface than ElevenLabs or Cartesia, and TTS-only, so pair it with something else for SFX and transcription. Set --workdir/-w (or WORKDIR) or audio lands in the system temp directory under /hume-tts; local playback wants ffplay or another CLI player on PATH. EMBEDDED_AUDIO_MODE (default false) returns audio inline instead, which is what you want in a client that cannot reach your filesystem.

servers.name: Ideogram MCP
servers.tagline: Official Ideogram server: bulk generation, editing, reframe, upscale and model training.
servers.description: Ideogram's official hosted MCP puts the Ideogram 4.x stack behind OAuth: bulk text-to-image, editing, reframing, upscaling, collections, and dataset upload plus custom model training. Ideogram remains the strongest engine for legible rendered text, which makes it the practical choice for title cards, posters, signage and any frame where type has to survive. The training tools matter for series work — teach it a show's typographic or graphic identity once, then generate against it.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add ideogram --transport http https://mcp.ideogram.ai/mcp

auth.key_url: OAuth: a browser window opens on first connect and you sign in with your Ideogram account

servers.notes: Usage draws on the same subscription as the Ideogram web app, so MCP jobs and hand work compete for one balance — the docs state flatly that there is no separate billing for MCP requests. Checked 9 Oct 2026: the endpoint is live and serves OAuth protected-resource metadata at the spec path, naming itself as the resource with an Ideogram-hosted authorization server and openid/email/profile scopes; the nine tools and the connect command below still match the docs verbatim. The MCP page now lists Ideogram 4.5 first, alongside 4.0, 3.0 and custom image models. The docs themselves point server-to-server pipelines at the REST API instead. This entry previously listed the community wrapper @sunwood-ai-labs/ideagram-mcp-server (MIT, 5 stars, one generate_image tool, untouched since May 2025, and misspelled 'ideagram' throughout) — it is superseded by the official server. Note that developer.ideogram.ai/_mcp/server is a separate documentation-search MCP, not the image server. Ideogram is also reachable via the fal and Replicate hub MCPs if you want fewer connectors.

servers.name: Imagine MCP
servers.tagline: One OAuth endpoint onto ImagineArt's video, image and music models — 96 tools, no keys.
servers.description: ImagineArt's official remote MCP exposes its whole generation catalogue through a single OAuth endpoint: text-to-video against Sora, Veo, Kling 3, Seedance, Runway, Hailuo, Wan and Luma; stills from Seedream, Flux, Imagen and Midjourney; plus music, upscaling, background removal and two guided pipelines (Ad Studio, Fashion Studio). For a filmmaker-agent it is a one-connection route to several flagship video models that have no first-party MCP, billed against one credit balance instead of six vendor accounts.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http imagine https://mcp.imagine.art

auth.key_url: Browser OAuth against an existing imagine.art account — no API key to generate or rotate; the endpoint's protected-resource metadata points at auth.vyro.ai with scopes openid, email and mcp:tools

servers.notes: Announced 15 Sep 2026, so this is a day-one listing — the endpoint is live and serves OAuth protected-resource metadata, but nothing here has been stress-tested across a production week. No free tier: ImagineArt's cheapest plan is Basic at $13/mo for 3,000 credits, and MCP calls draw on the same platform credits as the web app, so an agent on an empty balance gets nothing. The vendor claims 96 tools but publishes no tool list, hence tools_sample is null — run tools/list once connected. ImagineArt's own connect page documents the custom-connector UI rather than a CLI command; the claude mcp add form above is the standard HTTP-transport equivalent for the endpoint its metadata advertises (resource https://mcp.imagine.art/), not a command quoted from the vendor. Hard output ceilings to plan around: stills up to 4K, clips of five or ten seconds depending on the model, music around thirty seconds — this is a shot-generation hub, not a long-form tool. The vendor's own setup blog posts have already 410'd, which tells you something about the documentation's half-life. Broader, better-proven aggregators: fal, replicate, kie-ai.

servers.name: inference.sh MCP Server
servers.tagline: Official hosted hub: run any image, video, audio or 3D app, then poll the task.
servers.description: inference.sh's official streamable-HTTP server exposes its app catalogue as a small, generic tool set — list and inspect apps, run one, then track the task through logs, status and cancellation. The catalogue is the point for filmmakers: FLUX, GPT-Image-2, Veo 3, Seedance, Wan 2.7, ElevenLabs TTS and 3D generation behind one key, priced per run with the cost shown before you commit. It also proxies other MCP servers you have connected, so an agent can reach a generation app and a production tool through the same endpoint.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http inference https://api.inference.sh/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_INF_KEY"

auth.key_url: inference.sh workspace → Settings → API Keys (an inf_ prefixed token, sent as Authorization: Bearer)

servers.notes: Hosted only — no source repo for the server, and the inference-sh GitHub org publishes SDKs and example apps but nothing MCP. Registered in the official MCP Registry as ac.inference.sh/mcp, v2.0.1, published 27 Jul 2026 and marked active. The docs give a JSON client config rather than a CLI line; the claude_code command here is the standard header-remote translation of it. Auth is documented as a bearer inf_ key, but the endpoint also serves /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource naming itself as its own authorization server with apps:read and apps:execute scopes, so OAuth-capable clients may negotiate instead of taking a key — the key path is the one the docs actually support. Read the tool names before planning around them: this is a thin generic wrapper, so the model you want is a string argument to app_run, not its own tool, and there is no schema tool to check parameters before spending. Pricing is a subscription-plus-credits hybrid — free Starter tier, $20/mo Pro including $20 of credits — and per-run rates are steep at the top end, with video quoted from $0.05 to $17 per second. New to this directory and not yet exercised end to end here; for a broader catalogue with a documented schema tool, `fal` remains the safer default. Re-checked 7 Oct 2026: endpoint, bearer-key config and plan prices (Starter free, Pro $20, Team $200, each including matching credits) unchanged; the docs now also list knowledge_*, skill_* and mcp_* management tools alongside the app tools. The MCP Registry was unreachable that day, so the registry line above is from the previous check.

servers.name: invideo MCP Server
servers.tagline: Official remote MCP that turns a prompt into a scripted, narrated, subtitled cut.
servers.description: invideo's official hosted MCP hands an agent the whole assembly-line version of video: write the script from a prompt, pull clips from a stock library, lay in AI voiceover, and burn subtitles in 50+ languages, returning a full-length edit rather than a single shot. The entire surface is one tool — send a script plus topic, vibe, audience and platform, get a video URL back — so it is a blocking tool, not a finishing one: animatics, pitch reels, explainer inserts, and social cutdowns where speed beats frame-level control. Unlike almost every other server here it needs no key or account to connect, which makes it the cheapest thing to try and the hardest to reason about at scale.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http invideo https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp

auth.key_url: None — an unauthenticated initialize and tools/list both succeed against the endpoint

servers.notes: invideo pulled its MCP documentation some time between 17 Aug and 23 Sep 2026: help centre article 11316042 now 404s, the landing page at invideo.io/ai/mcp/ still links to it, and no replacement exists — the help centre's agent collections now cover the invideo Editor and its model line-up instead, with no MCP article among them. So `docs` is null: there is no published quota, credit model or transport guidance left to point at. The server outlived its docs and is in better shape than in August: on 23 Sep 2026 an unauthenticated POST to https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp completed a full handshake — Streamable HTTP, protocol 2024-11-05, serverInfo `invideo-ai` 0.0.2 — and returned tools/list, so the fields above now point there rather than at the deprecated /sse form, which still answers 200 if your client insists on SSE. That tools/list is the headline caveat: exactly one tool, `generate-video-from-script`, taking five required strings (script, topic, vibe, targetAudience, platform) and returning a video URL. No status tool, no shot control, no asset upload, no way to feed it your own footage. No auth also means no account linkage — expect anonymous rate limits, watermarking, or invideo-hosted output URLs whose lifecycle you do not own. Output is a templated stock-and-voiceover assembly; for shot-level generative control stay with the model servers in this category.

servers.name: json2video MCP
servers.tagline: Superseded community wrapper — JSON2Video now ships its own MCP.
servers.description: Community MCP wrapper for json2video.com: assemble scenes of video, images, text, HTML, voice, and subtitles as JSON and render server-side. JSON2Video has since shipped an official MCP of its own, listed here as `json2video-cli`, with thirteen tools against this one's four and a vendor keeping it current. This entry stays for the configs that already point at it; new pipelines should use the official server.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add json2video -e JSON2VIDEO_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY -- npx -y @omerrgocmen/json2video-mcp

auth.key_url: https://json2video.com

servers.notes: Use `json2video-cli` instead. Re-checked 31 Aug 2026 and nothing here has moved: still 26 stars, repo last pushed May 10 2025, npm @omerrgocmen/json2video-mcp still 1.3.1 from May 7 2025 — sixteen months untouched, and the GitHub repo carries no LICENSE file even though the npm manifest claims MIT. It still installs and json2video.com is still up, so it is not broken, merely abandoned. What changed is the alternative: JSON2Video published its own MCP inside the @json2video/cli package (Apr 2026), covering render, status, validation, templates, examples, account and full media-library management. Between an official server and a wrapper nobody has touched since the year before last, take the official one. Shotstack's official MCP, also in this directory, remains the other vendor-maintained route to cloud JSON video assembly.

servers.name: JSON2Video MCP
servers.tagline: The vendor's own MCP: render JSON movies, validate them, and manage the media library.
servers.description: JSON2Video's official MCP server, shipped as the `mcp` subcommand of its CLI. An agent describes a movie as JSON — scenes of video, images, text, HTML, voice-over and subtitles — validates it before spending credits, renders it server-side, then polls for the MP4. It also exposes the template catalogue and full media-library CRUD, which is what makes it usable for batch work: upload plates once, reference them across a hundred data-driven cuts without re-uploading.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add json2video -e JSON2VIDEO_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY -- npx -y @json2video/cli mcp

auth.key_url: https://json2video.com

servers.notes: Do not run `npx @json2video/mcp` — JSON2Video's own marketing page tells you to, and that package does not exist on npm (404). The working command is the CLI's subcommand, `npx -y @json2video/cli mcp`, which is what the actual MCP docs specify. The server is not open source: npm @json2video/cli is MIT-licensed but has no repository field and no public repo exists, so the thirteen tools listed in the docs are the only description of the surface you get. Two versions ever, 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 (Apr 14 2026), and nothing since — young and quiet rather than proven, though the API behind it is mature and the vendor advertises 99.9% uptime. Node >=20, stdio only, no hosted endpoint. Needs outbound HTTPS to api.json2video.com and cdn.json2video.com, which matters in locked-down CI. Free tier is 600 credits (~10 minutes of render); paid starts around $50/month, so make the agent call validate_movie before render_video — a malformed movie that fails late still costs you. `json2video auth` writes credentials to ~/.config/json2video/config.json instead of the env var; pick one and stay with it.

servers.name: Kie.ai MCP Server
servers.tagline: Run Veo, Seedance, Kling, Runway, Suno, ElevenLabs, FLUX and more through one local MCP.
servers.description: Community MCP server and sibling CLI for Kie.ai's media API, covering image, video, music and speech models from one connector — 38 tools across image, video, audio and task utilities. Since v4 it no longer fires generations directly: the agent drafts a plan with prepare_media_generation, a human approves it, and submit_media_generation spends the credits. For filmmaker-agents that buys a spend checkpoint in front of a broad model shelf, at the cost of an extra round trip per shot.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add kie-ai -e KIE_AI_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY -- npx -y @felores/kie-ai-mcp-server

auth.key_url: https://kie.ai/api-key

servers.notes: MIT, npm @felores/kie-ai-mcp-server still 5.0.0 (Aug 23 2026), Node >=20, 79 stars. The repo was last pushed Aug 26 2026 — Wan 3.0 support and a separate @felores/kie-ai-openai-server package (a loopback HTTP server with OpenAI-shaped image/video routes, not MCP) landed in the monorepo but not in a new MCP release, and it has been quiet for five weeks since. v4.0.0 (Aug 18) disabled direct media tool calls by default in favour of approval-bound plans: prepare_media_generation validates and creates no provider task, a host confirmation form or `kie-cli --approve <plan-id>` clears it, then submit_media_generation runs it. Set KIE_AI_ALLOW_DIRECT_GENERATION=true to restore the old one-shot behaviour, which is what unattended agents will need. v5.0.0 moved to the split SDK v2 packages and raised the floor to Node >=20 (npm engines; the release notes say the same), returns failures as isError with structuredContent, and gates official MCP Tasks behind KIE_AI_MCP_TASKS=true. Stdio by default, but v5 ships first-class HTTP: MCP_TRANSPORT=http or --http, with MCP_HTTP_HOST/MCP_HTTP_PORT and an optional KIE_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN bearer — self-hosted only via the Dockerfile and Coolify compose, there is no vendor-hosted URL. Filter the 38 tools with KIE_AI_ENABLED_TOOLS, KIE_AI_TOOL_CATEGORIES=image,video or KIE_AI_DISABLED_TOOLS (that precedence order) or you will burn context on unused schemas. Caveat: Kie.ai is an aggregator/reseller path for models from many vendors; rights, availability and ToS safety depend on the underlying provider, and Midjourney/Suno-style access should be treated as gray until verified for your use case.

servers.name: Kinocut
servers.tagline: Guardrailed local video editing MCP — FFmpeg, receipts, quality gates, and repurposing.
servers.description: Kinocut, formerly mcp-video, wraps FFmpeg and adjacent media tools behind typed, preflighted MCP operations, with a `kino` CLI and Python client over the same engine. For filmmaker agents it is the safer local post bench: inspect clips, trim and merge, burn captions, normalize audio, render variants, run release checkpoints, and fail early when an edit would produce bad media. Every operation writes a Video Receipt with input and output hashes so another agent or a human can verify what actually happened.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add kinocut -- uvx --from kinocut kino --mcp

servers.notes: Renamed: KyaniteLabs' mcp-video is now Kinocut. The slug here stays `mcp-video` so existing links keep resolving, but the project, package, CLI and docs have all moved. The old docs site kyanitelabs.github.io/mcp-video now 404s; product docs live at kinocut.dev. PyPI `mcp-video` is only a compatibility installer these days (1.6.16 pulls kinocut 1.16.1) — install `kinocut` and drive it with the `kino` CLI. The MCP server needs the `--mcp` flag (`kino --mcp`); this entry's install line omitted it before 9 Oct 2026, so bare `kino` configs copied from here will not start a server. Legacy `mcp_video` imports, MCP_VIDEO_* env vars, ~/.mcp-video data and mcp-video:// resource URIs are still honoured on the 1.14.x+ line, but that is a compatibility window, not a plan. Apache-2.0, 196 stars, Python >=3.11, v1.16.1 released Oct 5 2026, pushed Oct 9 2026, registered in the official MCP Registry as io.github.KyaniteLabs/kinocut; the README now names GitHub as canonical and the maintainer's Forgejo as a downstream mirror. Core editing needs FFmpeg on PATH and AI extras (Whisper, stems, upscalers, object matte) add gigabytes, so install only the extras you need; Hyperframes tools additionally want Node 22+. The 203-tool count is self-reported, and the README openly lists surfaces that are gated or unreleased — native desktop bundles are blocked on FFmpeg licensing, C2PA signing is development-tip only and off by default, and the trusted-execution kernel plus paid generative and dubbing plans are unshipped.

servers.name: Kling MCP
servers.tagline: Fullest direct Kling API MCP: video, extend, lip-sync, effects, KOLORS images.
servers.description: Community server hitting Kuaishou's official Kling API directly, with tools spanning text/image-to-video, video extension, lip-sync with TTS voices, effects, KOLORS image generation and virtual try-on. The most complete option if you want Kling on your own API account rather than via a hub.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add kling -e KLING_ACCESS_KEY=YOUR_KEY -e KLING_SECRET_KEY=YOUR_SECRET -- npx -y mcp-kling@latest

auth.key_url: https://app.klingai.com/global/dev/api-key

servers.notes: MIT, 41 stars. npm mcp-kling is at 5.2.0 (2025-12-22) while the public repo has not been pushed since 2025-06-14 — the published package is well ahead of the visible source, so read the npm tarball, not the README, for the current tool list. Largely superseded: Kling now runs its own hosted MCP at kling.ai/mcp (listed here as `kling-official`), which is OAuth, vendor-maintained and declares its model list at runtime. Keep this one if you need key/secret JWT auth against your own Kling API account, or the tools the official server does not expose — effects, virtual try-on and KOLORS. The README documents models through Kling v1.x/v2-master; for Kling 3.0 the official server, Runway, Higgsfield or the fal hub are all fresher. Auto-downloads results locally.

servers.name: Kling MCP (Official)
servers.tagline: Kling's own hosted MCP: text and image to video or stills, over OAuth on your Kling credits.
servers.description: Kuaishou now fronts Kling with a first-party remote MCP at kling.ai/mcp, replacing the key-and-secret dance the community servers require with browser OAuth. Eight tools cover text-to-image, image-to-image, text-to-video, image-to-video, file upload, task polling and credit balance, with the available models declared by the server at runtime rather than pinned in a README. For a filmmaker-agent this is the shortest verified path to current Kling models without going through a hub and paying a hub's markup.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http kling https://kling.ai/mcp

auth.key_url: Browser OAuth against https://kling.ai/auth — PKCE plus Dynamic Client Registration, scopes generation.create, generation.read and account.credit.read. No API key to paste.

servers.notes: Verified 2026-09-06 from primary sources only. https://kling.ai/mcp answers 401, and /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp names it as the resource behind authorization server https://kling.ai/auth; that server's metadata publishes authorization_code and refresh_token grants, S256 PKCE and a registration_endpoint, so DCR works and no pre-shared credential is needed. Tool names come from Kling's own npm package @klingai/cli-global (0.1.3, published by klingai-fe off a Kuaishou corp git remote), which calls itself a thin MCP client whose commands map 1:1 to backend MCP tools. Kling's setup page is a client-rendered app that returns nothing readable to a fetcher, so the CLI line above is the standard streamable-HTTP form of the documented endpoint, not a copy of a vendor one-liner — expect a browser authorization on first connect. Narrower than the community `kling` server: no effects, no virtual try-on, no KOLORS-specific tools, and no documented model list — call tool_list. Closed source, no public repo, and it spends the same Kling credits as the consumer platform.

servers.name: Krea MCP Server
servers.tagline: Official hosted MCP for Krea image/video models, schemas, uploads, and job widgets.
servers.description: Krea's official Streamable HTTP MCP lets agents discover available image and video models, inspect live input schemas, submit generation jobs, upload local assets, poll results, and cancel mistakes. For filmmakers it is a clean direct route into Krea's creative API and model shelf without hard-coding endpoints that drift. The MCP Apps widget can show an inline generation tile, auto-poll job progress, retry, cancel, and compare enhancement results in clients that support it.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http krea-ai https://api.krea.ai/mcp

auth.key_url: OAuth browser flow; API-token fallback from https://www.krea.ai/app/api/tokens sent as Authorization: Bearer.

servers.notes: Official hosted Streamable HTTP, endpoint answering with a 401 auth challenge as of Oct 3 2026; install command and seven tools unchanged. OAuth was added Jun 13 2026 and bills the workspace selected during consent; API-token auth still works for clients without OAuth but bills a separate workspace API balance, and cancelled jobs are not billed. Provider models disappear often and a sunset endpoint returns a terminal 410: video/openai/sora-2 and video/bytedance/seedance-1.0-lite went Apr 27 2026, image/bytedance/seedream-3 on May 13, Veo 2 and Veo 3 on Aug 28 (Veo 3.1 and 3.1 Lite remain), the Reve image models on Aug 31, and Kling 1.0, 1.5, 1.6, 2.0 Master and 2.1 on Sep 15. The developer deprecations page still lists only the first three; the later ones are in the changelog, so a pipeline pinned to an old Veo or Kling path is already broken. Deprecated endpoints send Deprecation: true and a Sunset header before they die. Have the agent call list_models/get_model_schema first — Krea surfaces deprecation metadata there and publishes no static model list, so the shelf is only knowable at runtime; the docs' own examples are image/krea/krea-2/medium and video/google/veo-3.1. get_upload_url returns presigned upload URLs valid for three hours. Docs moved from docs.krea.ai to www.krea.ai/docs.

servers.name: LeClap
servers.tagline: Deterministic video from one JSON template — same input, same frames, rendered locally.
servers.description: LeClap exposes its ffmpeg-video-composer engine over MCP: the agent asks for the template JSON Schema, authors a descriptor of sections, filters, music and text overlays, validates it for free, then renders it to an MP4 on the machine. Nothing is sampled and nothing is uploaded, so the same template produces the same frames on every run — the opposite trade to a generative model, and the right one for titles, lower thirds, and any card you will need to re-render at 3am with one word changed. An opt-in bridge renders compositions from your own Remotion project into a clip the deterministic engine then composites.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add leclap -e LECLAP_MCP_MEDIA_DIR=/abs/path/to/media -e LECLAP_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR=/abs/path/to/renders -- npx -y @leclap/mcp

servers.notes: First-party to the LeClap project — the MCP package lives in its monorepo — but that project is one maintainer's open-source work, not a company, so it is listed as community. MIT, 24 stars on the monorepo, npm @leclap/mcp 0.3.4 (24 Aug 2026), listed in the official MCP registry as dev.leclap/video. Node >=24.11.0 — an unusually aggressive floor that will bounce most CI images and any Node 22 LTS setup. FFmpeg is not bundled for the npx path: the engine looks for a system binary first and falls back to an optional `ffmpeg-static` that `npx -y @leclap/mcp` will not install for you, so put ffmpeg on PATH. Set LECLAP_MCP_MEDIA_DIR deliberately — local inputs must resolve inside it via a symlink-safe containment check, and pointing it at your home directory hands every tool call the run of it. `render_remotion_clip` runs your project's own JavaScript under headless Chromium and is therefore off unless you pass --allow-remotion; it also needs @remotion/renderer and @remotion/bundler installed yourself, and Remotion's own licence applies. Determinism is per platform, not across them — Node and browser encode with libx264, Android with libopenh264, iOS with h264_videotoolbox, and the on-device build silently drops boxblur and rewrites eq to lutyuv. There is no template catalogue; the server authors descriptors from the schema. Renders are 10-minute-capped by default. The MCP package is under a month old — read it as promising, not proven.

servers.name: Luma AI MCP Server
servers.tagline: Community MCP with the widest tool surface on Luma's legacy Dream Machine API.
servers.description: Community Python server for Luma's Dream Machine API v1: text/image-to-video on ray-2 and ray-flash-2, video extension and interpolation, Photon image generation, upscaling, audio addition and credit checks. Luma has since moved its platform to the Agents API — uni-1 and uni-1-max for images, ray-3.2 for video, a new base URL and a new key name — which this server does not speak and for which no MCP exists. Its reason to exist next to Luma's own `luma-official` server is breadth: extension, interpolation, upscaling and credit checks that the first-party two-tool server never shipped.

auth.key_url: https://lumalabs.ai/dream-machine/api — the Agents API uses a different key under LUMA_AGENTS_API_KEY at agents.lumalabs.ai/v1

servers.notes: Correction on 2026-09-08: this entry previously called the repo MIT and claimed it was the only Luma server in MCP form. Neither holds — there is no LICENSE file in the repo and GitHub reports no license, so the code is technically all-rights-reserved, and Luma's own lumalabs/luma-api-mcp exists (listed here as `luma-official`). Tiny (6 stars) and last committed 2025-04-01 — functional rather than maintained; runs from a cloned repo via uv. Kept listed because nothing has been switched off: api.lumalabs.ai/dream-machine/v1/ping still returns 200 as of 2026-09-08. Luma publishes no MCP server for the Agents API, so ray-3.2 and uni-1 are reachable only over REST or the Go/Python/JS SDKs, or through fal, Replicate and Runway hub MCPs.

servers.name: Luma API MCP
servers.tagline: Luma's own two-tool MCP server for Ray video and Photon stills.
servers.description: Luma Labs' first-party MCP server, published from the lumalabs GitHub org, exposing exactly two tools: create_image on photon-1 and photon-flash-1, and create_video on ray-2, ray-flash-2 and ray-1-6. create_video takes frame0 and frame1 references, so an agent can pin both ends of a shot and chain continuity across a sequence; create_image accepts image, style, character and modify references for consistent looks. auth.key_url: https://lumalabs.ai/api/keys

servers.notes: Official but frozen: MIT, 26 stars, 12 forks, created 2025-04-15 and last pushed 2025-04-18, two open issues, no releases and no package on PyPI. It speaks the Dream Machine API only — Luma's current Agents API (uni-1, uni-1-max, ray-3.2 at agents.lumalabs.ai/v1 under LUMA_AGENTS_API_KEY) is not supported here or in any other MCP server. The documented install path only writes Claude Desktop's config file; there is no vendor-published `claude mcp add` form, hence the null above rather than a command we made up. For a wider Dream Machine tool surface use the community `luma` server; for ray-3.2 today, reach it through the fal, Replicate or Runway hub MCPs.

servers.name: Magic Hour MCP
servers.tagline: Magic Hour's hosted MCP: 44 tools across video, image and voice generation on one connection.
servers.description: Magic Hour's first-party remote server is generated from its OpenAPI spec with FastMCP, so every public endpoint arrives as a tool: text-, image- and video-to-video, lip sync, talking photos, face and character replacement, auto subtitles, image generation, editing, upscaling and background removal, plus voice generation and cloning. Creation tools return a project id and the credits charged immediately, and matching wait_for_*_project tools poll to completion and hand back exact signed download URLs. For a filmmaker-agent it is a broad single-vendor toolbox with the async plumbing already worked out.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --scope user --transport http magic-hour https://mcp.magichour.ai/ --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_MAGIC_HOUR_API_KEY"

auth.key_url: https://magichour.ai/developer?tab=api-keys — Claude Code and Codex send it as a bearer header; Claude desktop connectors run an OAuth flow (client ID magic-hour-mcp) whose authorization page asks you to paste the same key.

servers.notes: Verified live 2026-09-15: initialize answered protocol 2025-06-18 as magic-hour 0.1.0, and an unauthenticated tools/list returned all 44 tools — discovery is public, calls need the key. The connect line is copied from magichour.ai/mcp. The OAuth is a shim, not delegated auth: mcp.magichour.ai names itself as both protected resource and authorization server, and the flow validates an API key and uses it as the access token, so the agent holds a full-account credential either way. Money: the same credits as the web app, $1 buys 400 in packs or 144k to 840k a year on the $12 to $66 monthly plans, and the pricing page lists API access as a paid-plan feature — we did not confirm that a free account can mint a working key. The server is a thin generated layer over the REST API, so tool names are long operationId-style strings and quality is whatever Magic Hour's underlying models deliver; the vendor's own setup page says only Claude, Claude Code and Codex are verified clients. The repo has no licence file and 6 stars, but the GitHub org dates from 2023 and the submitter's account states Magic Hour employment.

servers.name: Magnific MCP
servers.tagline: Official remote MCP for upscaling, image/video generation, characters, and asset history.
servers.description: Magnific's official remote MCP connects agents to its creative upscaler, image generation/editing, video generation, Soul character/style references, creation history, TTS, and 3D model generation through one OAuth endpoint. For filmmakers, it is strongest as a remote polish-and-iteration bench: upscale keeper frames, crop or relight plates, train reusable references, then browse prior generations without leaving the chat.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http magnific https://mcp.magnific.com

auth.key_url: OAuth with a Magnific account; no API key is needed for MCP.
