Remote streamable HTTP only; no local package or source repo is published for the official MCP, and a plain browser GET on the endpoint just redirects to the web app. The docs say tools draw from the same Magnific credit balance as the app/API, and live `tools/list` is the source of truth — the published catalogue is still grouped by domain (account, creations, image generation and editing, video, audio, 3D, custom references, folders and spaces, discovery) rather than enumerated tool by tool. The MCP surface is broader than pure upscaling — image/video generation, Soul references, TTS, 3D, folders, and prior-creation browsing — so use explicit prompts when you want faithful enhancement rather than creative reinterpretation.

servers.name: MakeAIVideo MCP
servers.tagline: Brief or script in, narrated and captioned MP4 out, over one OAuth endpoint.
servers.description: MakeAIVideo's official hosted MCP turns a one-line brief, a supplied script, or a still image into a finished video — script, neural voiceover, generated scenes, caption timing, music bed and MP4 export in a single pass. The endpoint advertises 39 tools covering render, script authoring, scene and voice regeneration, captions, share links, ideas, characters and portraits, voices, music, brand kit and webhooks. For a filmmaker-agent this is the assembly end of the pipeline: explainers, spokesperson cuts and vertical social edits where finishing speed matters more than shot-level control.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --scope user --transport http makeaivideo https://mcp.makeaivideo.ai

auth.key_url: Browser approval during connector setup (dynamic client registration + PKCE), or a mav_* key from Settings → Advanced → API keys

servers.notes: Brand new: version 1.2.0 was published to the official MCP registry on 4 Sep 2026 and listed here the next day, so there is no maintenance record yet — re-verify before you build a paid pipeline on it. The vendor names no company, no jurisdiction and no repo, and describes its engines only as 'a curated stack of leading AI models', so you cannot audit which model renders your footage or what the output licence is. tools_sample stays null because the 39 tools are counted but not enumerated anywhere public; call tools/list after connecting. Unauthenticated calls return JSON-RPC error -32001 rather than an HTTP 401, which trips clients that key off status codes. OAuth carries read/write/ai scopes; the optional Bearer mav_* key is the fallback for headless clients. An assistant spends the same credits you do, and there is no free tier past the 7-day trial — plans start at $9/month for 450 credits. Overlaps heavily with invideo: both are templated script-to-video assemblers, and invideo costs nothing to try while this one has a real endpoint and real auth.

servers.name: Martini
servers.tagline: The film set for AI videos — direct entire productions from your agent.
servers.description: Martini is the command surface for agentic filmmaking: one MCP connection that puts an entire film set — the latest video models, infinite production canvases, consistent characters, and a real timeline — under your agent's direction. It is an open platform, agent-friendly by design: the MCP server is a first-class product surface rather than an integration afterthought, so any MCP-capable agent (Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, Gemini CLI, or one you built) gets the same full control of the set that the UI offers. The model roster stays current, and the server resolves natural-language model requests to the right engine. Fifty-nine registered tools span the pipeline: project and board context, reusable subjects and collections, prompt variables, frame extraction for shot chaining, image upload, multi-track timeline context and edits, model/job lookup, and approved generation with cost confirmation. Over 200 professional films have been made on Martini — aired as TV commercials, shown as artwork, and gone viral.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user martini https://www.martini.film/mcp

auth.key_url: https://www.martini.film — sign in with your Martini account

servers.notes: Remote MCP server maintained first-party by Martini (YC-backed), with live production endpoint https://www.martini.film/mcp returning OAuth protected-resource metadata and a Supabase-backed bearer challenge — re-confirmed 21 Sep 2026, and the install command above is the one the vendor's own Claude Code page prints. The 59-tool figure in the description comes from the backend source read in June 2026 and is not independently checkable from outside: the public docs publish a representative table of roughly 40 read and write tools and state explicitly that it is not the complete catalogue, so treat live `tools/list` as the count that matters. The narrower core profile the docs still advertise at https://www.martini.film/mcp-core — the same project, board, canvas, subject, upload, download, review and organization tools minus direct generation, for clients or directories that disallow AI media generation — did not answer as an MCP endpoint on 21 Sep 2026: POST initialize returns the marketing page as 200 text/html instead of JSON-RPC, on both the apex and www hosts, and the site's protected-resource metadata declares only https://www.martini.film/mcp. Use the full endpoint until that is fixed. Generation tools require explicit user approval of model, prompt, count, target shot, and estimated olive cost before spending credits. Public setup docs now cover Claude Desktop/Web, Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Hermes, OpenClaw, and generic Streamable HTTP clients.

servers.name: MaxVideoAI
servers.tagline: Quote a shot across the video model zoo, then approve the one you want to pay for.
servers.description: Hosted AI video and image production with model comparison, project budgeting, exact quotes and result recovery in a shared library. The packaged plan and generate skills orchestrate distinct MCP tools rather than being the names of the remote tools themselves. A filmmaker can compare the cost of a shot list before preparing a concrete request; submitting one paid attempt requires explicit approval of its exact quote.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http maxvideoai https://api.maxvideoai.com/mcp

auth.key_url: https://maxvideoai.com

servers.notes: Requires a MaxVideoAI account and browser OAuth. The public Glama connector reports 15 tools and authenticated healthy status as of 19 Sep 2026; this is tool-discovery evidence, not an independent paid-generation test. If a conversation is interrupted after a job was accepted, recover that job with get_generation_status or list_recent_generations before considering another submission. A new paid attempt needs a fresh quote and explicit approval; recovering an accepted job does not. Host-specific reference import and inline playback support vary, so follow the current setup documentation. The public repository contains the client/plugin package, not a self-hostable server, and uses Business Source License 1.1. Promptibus, also in this directory, covers model pricing intelligence without asking for an account.

servers.name: Maya MCP Server
servers.tagline: Drive live Autodesk Maya sessions from an agent — arbitrary Python, streamed back.
servers.description: A stdio MCP server that talks to running Maya sessions over Maya's Python command port, with no plugin to install inside Maya itself. Rather than a fixed tool menu it hands the agent `execute_code` and `write_module`, so anything the Maya Python API can do is reachable and output streams back as it runs. It also scans for sessions as artists open and close them, so one server can address several Mayas at once — useful when layout, animation and lighting are open side by side.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport stdio maya -- uvx maya-mcp-server
install.stdio_command: uvx maya-mcp-server (or `pip install maya-mcp-server`); first enable the port inside Maya with cmds.commandPort(name=":7002", sourceType="python")

auth.key_url: No key; needs a running Maya with its Python command port open — put the commandPort call in userSetup.py to make it automatic

servers.notes: Maya is still the last major DCC in this directory without a first-party MCP — Autodesk's public MCP servers target Revit, Fusion and its data APIs, not the M&E line — and the community field is fragmented rather than deep. Checked 29 Sep 2026: this repo is MIT, 42 stars, but has not been pushed since 15 Jul 2026, so it is a quiet project rather than a maintained product. The gap between repo and release persists: PyPI maya-mcp-server is still 0.1.0 from 5 Jan 2026, so `uvx maya-mcp-server` gets you January's code; clone and `uv run --directory` if you want current. The design trade is the whole story — `execute_code` is arbitrary Python inside your Maya session, which is why the tool count is four instead of three hundred, and also why you should not point it at a scene you cannot afford to lose. The command port is unauthenticated on localhost. Alternatives if you want typed tools instead: dcc-mcp/dcc-mcp-maya is now the most active (MIT, 57 stars, pushed 29 Sep 2026, Maya 2020+, ~79 typed tools) but is a different shape — `mayapy -m pip install dcc-mcp-maya` plus a Maya plug-in that fronts a Rust HTTP sidecar, rather than a zero-install command-port client; GimbalGoats/GG_MayaMCP (MIT, 23 stars, last pushed 14 Aug 2026, Maya 2024+); and PatrickPalmer/MayaMCP (MIT, 104 stars but frozen since May 2025 — the one Griptape's docs still point at).

servers.name: mediagen
servers.tagline: One MCP across Gemini, OpenAI and Kie AI, with EU AI Act disclosure marking built in.
servers.description: A single Node package that ships as a CLI, a Claude Code skill and an MCP server, fronting Google Gemini (Nano Banana stills up to 4K, plus video), OpenAI's gpt-image and DALL-E, and roughly thirty Kie AI models including Flux, Imagen and Grok. The MCP surface is deliberately narrow — one generate call, one model list, one config check — so an agent picks a model by name rather than learning three vendor APIs. What sets it apart for anyone shipping into Europe is the marking step: it writes IPTC/XMP DigitalSourceType into outputs and can composite the official EU AI Act label onto a frame, which no other server in this directory does.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add mediagen --env GEMINI_API_KEY=your-api-key-here -- npx -y mediagen mcp

auth.key_url: Bring your own provider keys — GEMINI_API_KEY is the minimum, OPENAI_API_KEY and KIE_API_KEY are optional; `mediagen init` walks through configuration

servers.notes: New and unproven: the repo was created 22 Aug 2026, all of its ~39 commits landed inside a single day, and there has been no push since 23 Aug. 54 stars, MIT, CI green, zero open issues, npm mediagen 0.3.0. Listed for the marking feature, not for its track record — check the commit log before you build a pipeline on it. The disclosure marking is CLI-only (`mediagen mark`) and the docs state it is never automatic, so an agent generating through the MCP tools gets no provenance metadata unless something calls the CLI afterwards. Video is Gemini-only; OpenAI and Kie AI cover stills and edits. The package is free but every generation bills the provider key you supply, and Kie AI is itself an aggregator — if you only want breadth of models, the kie-ai or fal entries here are the more direct route.

servers.name: Meshy MCP Server
servers.tagline: Official Meshy MCP — generate, retexture, rig, and animate 3D models via API.
servers.description: Meshy's official MCP server with 24 tools spanning text/image-to-3D generation, remeshing, retexturing, rigging, animation, UV unwrap, format conversion, and task management. For filmmakers it turns character and prop creation — including rigged, animatable assets — into an agent call, with no DCC required on the machine.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add-json meshy '{"command":"npx","args":["-y","@meshy-ai/meshy-mcp-server"],"env":{"MESHY_API_KEY":"msy_YOUR_API_KEY"}}'

auth.key_url: https://www.meshy.ai/settings/api

servers.notes: Official (meshy-dev org), MIT, TypeScript, stdio and HTTP transports; npm @meshy-ai/meshy-mcp-server is now 0.5.1 (27 Aug 2026), repo pushed 22 Aug 2026. Only 40 stars — vendor-maintained rather than community-loved, so judge it on the push cadence, which is good. v0.5.0 added Meshy 7 (`ai_model: "meshy-7"`), an `ultra_mode` high-detail pass, Smart Topology, 8K textures and multi-view retexture, and grew Creative Lab to seven products. Two traps in that: `meshy-7` is accepted on image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d and retexture but **not** on text-to-3d, where `latest` still resolves to Meshy 6; and the old `hd_texture` flag is deprecated in favour of `texture_resolution`. API access requires a Meshy Pro plan or above, and every call spends credits — image-to-3D is 20 for mesh and 30 textured on meshy-6/7 (35 at 8K), while `model_type: "smart-topology"` with meshy-t2 drops that to 5/15/20 and returns part-separated geometry, which is the cheapest useful path for previz props. ultra_mode adds 5, Creative Lab is 36 (62 for keycap), remesh 5, rig 5, animate 3, convert 1, resize 1, uv-unwrap 5, repair-printability 10, multicolor 10. Budget before you loop an agent over it.

servers.name: MiniMax MCP
servers.tagline: Official MiniMax server: Hailuo video, image gen, TTS and voice cloning.
servers.description: MiniMax's official MCP server exposes Hailuo video generation, text-to-image, and best-in-class multilingual TTS with voice cloning and voice design. One vendor and one key covers both your shots and your dialogue — rare breadth for a single official server. Music generation was part of that breadth until August 2026, when the tool was retired.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add minimax -e MINIMAX_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY -e MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://api.minimax.io -- uvx minimax-mcp

auth.key_url: https://platform.minimax.io — key region must match MINIMAX_API_HOST (api.minimax.io global / api.minimaxi.com mainland) or auth fails

servers.notes: MIT, 1,576 stars, with an official JS sibling (MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-MCP-JS, 128 stars, pushed 2026-08-21). The three-month quiet spell ended on 2026-08-20: the server migrated to MCP Python SDK v2 and **retired the `music_generation` tool** in the same batch, shipped as PyPI minimax-mcp 0.0.19 on 2026-08-21. Score elsewhere — Mureka, Sonilo or Epidemic Sound. `play_audio` survives in the code but has been dropped from the README's tool table, so treat it as undocumented rather than guaranteed. Watch the model drift: the default text-to-video model constant is now `MiniMax-Hailuo-2.3`, while `generate_video`'s own tool description still enumerates only up to `MiniMax-Hailuo-02` and the older T2V/I2V-01 Director line — an agent reading the schema will not know what it is actually being given. Default speech model is `speech-2.8-hd`. image_to_video is JS-only. The README now steers you to MiniMax's `mmx-cli` agent skill ahead of this server, which is the vendor telling you where the newest models land first. MINIMAX_API_RESOURCE_MODE toggles URL vs local-file output; MINIMAX_MCP_BASE_PATH sets the output directory.

servers.name: Mirelo MCP
servers.tagline: Foley generated against the picture, then extended or patched region by region.
servers.description: Mirelo's official remote MCP exposes its SFX V1 video-to-audio model: hand it a clip and it reads the on-screen action, motion and pacing and generates effects synced to what it sees, with an optional text prompt to steer the character of the sound. Text-to-sound covers the cues with no plate, and two repair tools matter more than they sound — extend a bed that came back short, or inpaint one region of a clip while leaving the rest untouched, so a single bad hit does not cost the whole pass. A preflight estimate returns credits and runtime before it generates, which is what makes batching a folder of shots safe.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http mirelo https://mcp.mirelo.ai/mcp

auth.key_url: https://mirelo.ai — browser 'Sign in with Mirelo'; no API key, and OAuth client ID/secret are left empty when adding it as a custom connector

servers.notes: Announced 30 Jul 2026; hosted endpoint still answering with a 401 challenge on 3 Oct 2026, install command unchanged. Billed against the same Studio credits as the Mirelo web app, so it needs an account with balance — the preflight tool is worth calling first. Limits Mirelo states outright: music generation and multi-stem generation are not exposed in MCP v1, and result download links are temporary, so an agent that generates without saving loses the take. In Claude (web and Desktop), file uploads fail until you allowlist studio-project-assets.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com under Settings → Capabilities — the usual reason a video-to-SFX call never sees the clip. Documented clients are Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and ChatGPT; Codex has its own `codex mcp add mirelo --url https://mcp.mirelo.ai/mcp` plus `codex mcp login mirelo`. Tool names are not published — call tools/list. Closest comparisons here are ElevenLabs text_to_sound_effects and Sonilo's video_to_sfx; Mirelo is the narrower specialist, and region-level inpainting is the thing neither of those offers.

servers.name: Miro MCP
servers.tagline: Official Miro MCP — build and read storyboards, frames, and planning boards via AI.
servers.description: Miro's hosted MCP server (public beta) lets agents create and read board content, now through an SVG canvas model: the agent writes a board by sending SVG and reads one back the same way, alongside tools to create and search boards, place images, and work prototypes and comments. A strong fit for storyboard layouts, shot-planning walls, and mood boards your whole team can see.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http miro https://mcp.miro.com

auth.key_url: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration; run /mcp auth in Claude Code and complete the Miro browser flow

servers.notes: The tool surface was rebuilt since we last checked, so cached configs and prompts will break. Miro's tools page now documents an SVG canvas model — canvas_create_from_svg, canvas_read_as_svg, canvas_update_from_svg and a canvas_get_canvas_composer_skill helper — and states that board_list_items and the whole context_*, layout_*, diagram_* and doc_* families were removed; table_create, table_list_rows and table_sync_rows are marked deprecating soon. Practical effect for storyboards: you no longer place sticky notes and frames item by item, you hand the server SVG. Still public beta more than seven months after the 2 Feb 2026 launch — the Claude Code marketplace listing still says 'MCP is in Public Beta', even though developers.miro.com now leads with 'works for all Miro plans, even free teams'. Enterprise remains the catch: that listing says an Enterprise admin must enable MCP before anyone can authorize. Endpoint re-confirmed 20 Sep 2026 as https://mcp.miro.com (Miro's connect docs write it with a trailing slash; both forms are in Miro's own material). The Claude Code plugin route needs two commands, not one — /plugin marketplace add miroapp/miro-ai then /plugin install miro@miro-ai — and it ships three skills (miro-code-review, miro-code-spec, miro-code-explain-on-board) that are engineering-facing rather than film-facing. miroapp/miro-ai is alive: 154 stars, last push 17 Sep 2026. Tool names above are from developers.miro.com/docs/miro-mcp-tools — the server's own tools/list is the source of truth.

servers.name: Mosaic Motion MCP
servers.tagline: Hosted motion-design agent: a prompt in, a finished animated MP4 out, refined by follow-ups.
servers.description: Mosaic Motion is an agent that turns a brief into a finished motion-design video — typography, layout, animation, voiceover — and its official hosted MCP exposes that as a job queue: create a video from a prompt with up to 100 attachments, poll the session, then refine the result with follow-up prompts instead of re-rolling. It renders 16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:5 and 21:9 at lengths from under ten seconds to a few minutes. For a film pipeline this is not shot generation; it is the graphics department — title cards, logo stings, explainer inserts, launch and festival promo pieces — handed to an agent that can iterate on notes.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http motion https://mcp.motion.so/mcp

auth.key_url: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration on first connect (sign up at https://motion.so); headless agents can use the device flow at https://motion.so/device, a service account, or a Motion API key sent as Authorization: Bearer

servers.notes: Read the tool list before you connect it: besides generation, the MCP exposes `purchase_credits`, `subscribe_to_plan`, `setup_payment_method` and `set_auto_topup`, and its OAuth metadata advertises `motion:credits:purchase` and `motion:account:manage` scopes. The docs say a purchase completes immediately if a payment method is on file, so decline those scopes or keep a card off the account unless you want the agent spending on its own. Pricing is $5 per 200 credits, which the docs equate to only one or two videos; longer videos, premium models, voiceover and follow-up edits all cost more, and no free allotment is documented. The docs also contradict themselves: the API overview says purchasing and top-ups are web-app only, while the MCP and credits guides list tools for both. It is a brand and marketing product at heart — launch videos, product demos, logo animations — so expect a house look tuned for SaaS promos, not grade-matched titles for a feature. Output is MP4 at a resolution the docs don't state, with no project-file or layered export documented. Checked 27 Sep 2026: https://mcp.motion.so/mcp serves live OAuth protected-resource metadata naming Claude Code among its expected clients, but this pass did not complete a tools/list call, so the tool names come from the vendor guide. No public source repo. The name collides with Motion (usemotion.com), the unrelated calendar app that also has MCP servers, so check the domain before you install.

servers.name: Movie Scene Map (formerly FilmMap)
servers.tagline: Where films and series were actually shot: 31,000+ locations in 177 countries, from Wikidata.
servers.description: A read-only remote MCP over a Wikidata-derived atlas of filming locations — 31,115 places across 177 countries, tied to 19,707 films and series plus 2,153 video games and the indexed anime and manga. An agent can ask where a production was shot, what was shot at a given place, search by coordinates and radius, or rank the most-filmed locations in a country. For recce and reference it answers the question a location scout starts with: who has already shot here, and what did it look like on screen. No signup, no key, no install — point a client at the endpoint and query.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http moviescenemap https://moviescenemap.com/mcp

servers.notes: Renamed: FilmMap became Movie Scene Map on 1 September 2026, and thefilmmap.com now 301s to moviescenemap.com. The repo README (re-checked 2026-10-01; pushed 2026-09-08, MIT, still 0 stars, one personal account) names https://moviescenemap.com/mcp as the endpoint and says the old https://thefilmmap.com/mcp keeps answering for clients configured before the rename — but the official MCP registry still lists com.thefilmmap/filming-locations v1.1.0 at the old address, so registry-driven clients will be pointed there until it is republished. Stateless streamable HTTP, POST-only; a GET returning 405 is correct. The docs publish a JSON client config rather than a per-client command; the claude mcp add line above is that endpoint in Claude Code form. The atlas roughly doubled with the rename (31,115 locations, 177 countries, per the data page) and counts move with every deploy — trust get_statistics over any figure quoted here. Read the medium distinction before quoting anything: films and series carry real filming locations (Wikidata P915), while games, anime and manga carry narrative settings (P840) and were filmed nowhere, and the server labels each record so an agent does not conflate them. Some links now come from a production's English Wikipedia Filming section rather than Wikidata; those arrive in separate fields under CC BY-SA 4.0 and must be cited as 'per Wikipedia'. Coverage is uneven — some productions are placed at country level only, and the unplaceable ones are listed at moviescenemap.com/gaps/. A place is not a scene: there is no shot-level granularity, so this narrows a recce list, it does not replace one. The factual dataset is CC0; Commons photographs and some city permit datasets keep their own attribution terms.

servers.name: Mureka MCP
servers.tagline: Official Mureka server for lyrics, songs, and instrumental background music.
servers.description: Mureka's official MCP server lets agents generate lyrics, turn lyrics into songs, and create instrumental background music through the Mureka API, saving audio files locally. For a filmmaker-agent it is a first-party alternative to Suno resellers when you need temp songs, cue sketches, or quick underscore drafts without the licensing cloud hanging over them.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add mureka -e MUREKA_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY -e MUREKA_API_URL=https://api.mureka.ai -- uvx mureka-mcp

auth.key_url: https://platform.mureka.ai/apiKeys

servers.notes: Official and MIT, but effectively abandoned as a package: PyPI mureka-mcp 0.0.13 and the last repo commit are both 13 May 2025 — sixteen months untouched at 116 stars. Community PRs are piling up unreviewed, including one opened 27 Aug 2026 to declare the missing httpx dependency and pin mcp to v1 — a hint that a fresh uvx install may resolve dependencies the code was never tested against. The wider Mureka API has since grown prompt-to-song, soundtrack, stems, remix, region editing and TTS endpoints; this MCP still exposes only four tools. Credits required. Confirmed in the source: audio saves to $HOME/Desktop unless MUREKA_MCP_BASE_PATH is set, and TIME_OUT_SECONDS defaults to 60 — far too short for a full song, so raise it (the README's own example uses 300) before any production run.

servers.name: Mux MCP Server
servers.tagline: Official Mux MCP: upload, manage, and analyze video via API or hosted remote server.
servers.description: The official MCP server for the full Mux Video + Mux Data platform: upload videos, create and manage assets and live streams, mint playback IDs, manage webhooks, and query video performance analytics. Available both as a hosted remote at mcp.mux.com (OAuth, pick your environment) and as the @mux/mcp npm package — the strongest official offering in video infrastructure. Its two tools are a docs search (search_docs) and a sandboxed TypeScript executor over the Mux SDK, so the whole API surface is reachable without hundreds of tool definitions.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http mux https://mcp.mux.com

auth.key_url: Remote: OAuth via dashboard.mux.com. Local: MUX_TOKEN_ID + MUX_TOKEN_SECRET from dashboard.mux.com → Settings → Access Tokens

servers.notes: npm @mux/mcp v15.3.0 (released 2026-09-23), Apache-2.0, source at muxinc/mux-ts under packages/mcp-server, and the repo is still pushed weekly. The tool is named search_docs, per both the source and Mux's docs; earlier listings here called it docs_search. The other tool is execute, which runs TypeScript against the @mux/ts SDK in an isolated sandbox. That two-tool 'Code Mode' design is unchanged and covers the whole API without hundreds of per-endpoint tools. Since v15.0 the package ships a second binary, mcp-code-runner, which v15.2 made resolve Deno via DENO_PATH or a bundled binary. The desktop bundle ships without Deno, so point DENO_PATH at one if local execute fails. v15.3 dropped the 'Experimental' label from Mux Robots (captions, chapters). The hosted remote falls back to Basic auth (base64 token ID:secret in the Authorization header) for clients without OAuth. v15.0 remains the breaking release: @mux/mux-node became @mux/ts (the old name is an alias), client.robotsPreview became client.robots, and the deprecated Data filters/exports endpoints are gone. Code written against v14 needs MIGRATION.md.

servers.name: Nomi
servers.tagline: Open-source desktop workbench your agent directs: storyboard, generate, cut on a timeline.
servers.description: Nomi is a local-first Electron workbench that exposes its own production surface over MCP, so Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, or WorkBuddy can create a project, lay out shots on a canvas, draft and price a generation, clear a paid confirmation gate, and land the result on an editable timeline. The model layer is bring-your-own: hosted providers come pre-wired, and anything OpenAI-compatible or a local ComfyUI graph slots in beside them. That combination is rare — most studio-tier servers in this directory are hosted products that own the models, whereas here the agent directs software on your own machine against whatever engines you are already paying for. Durable production runs make it more than fire-and-forget: the agent can start a run, review and revise scripts and storyboards, and decide creative gates, while budget, export, and publishing stay with the human in the app.

install.stdio_command: Multi-step: install the Nomi desktop app (Nomi-mac-arm64.dmg, Nomi-mac-x64.dmg, or Nomi-windows-setup.exe from GitHub Releases), launch it once so it mints the local token, then use Model Integration > Connect AI Programming Assistant to register the bundled stdio server with your client. Do not hand-write the config: Nomi signs a per-machine, per-client proof into it. No published `claude mcp add` one-liner.

auth.key_url: No key for the MCP link — a local token is written to ~/.nomi/capability-core/token on first launch. Model providers still need their own API keys, entered in the app.

servers.notes: The tool surface was rebuilt in September, so older configs and saved prompts will not match it. The docs now count 24 tools, collapsed from 42 one-verb tools on 2 Sep 2026. Every read goes through `nomi_read`, canvas writes go through `nomi_canvas_edit` under a project lease, and a single generation is plan → preview → gate → execute. The `nomi_generate`, `nomi_add_nodes` and `nomi_get_run` names this entry used to list are gone. `nomi_canvas_plan` was retired on 5 Sep and `nomi_layout_read`/`nomi_layout_write` on 14 Sep. You can no longer copy the config between machines or clients: Nomi writes signed `NOMI_MCP_CLIENT` / `NOMI_MCP_CLIENT_PROOF` values bound to one machine and one client. A bare `NOMI_MCP_STDIO=1` entry can still list tools, but Nomi treats it as `external` and it cannot start real production runs. The old scripts/nomi-mcp.mjs path now exits with a migration message. By design the agent cannot approve budgets, per-shot paid submits, rough-cut acceptance, export or publishing. Those decisions come back to the app. Very active: ~520 stars, v0.22.1 released 26 Sep 2026, pushed 27 Sep 2026. It is still a single personal GitHub account, not an org. Licence: AGPL-3.0 for current releases, with a separate commercial licence on request, so shipping a derivative product means negotiating a licence first. Desktop-only: macOS arm64/x64 plus Windows x64, no Linux build. Releases now include electron-updater manifests. This pass did not recheck whether the builds are code-signed; earlier ones were not. The MCP guide is Chinese-only. 'Local-first' covers projects, assets and keys, but the guide itself notes that prompts and inputs still go to whichever provider you configured, and every generation bills that provider's key.

servers.name: Notion MCP
servers.tagline: Notion's hosted MCP: search, read, and write docs, wikis, and databases via OAuth.
servers.description: Notion's official hosted MCP server gives agents OAuth-scoped access to a workspace: keyword search over pages and people, a separate AI search that reaches connected sources when the workspace has Notion AI, fetch of pages and databases, and create/update content through AI-native, Markdown-first tools. The natural home for script drafts, beat sheets, character bibles, and shot lists an agent can read and update.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp

auth.key_url: One-click OAuth at mcp.notion.com; local server uses a NOTION_TOKEN integration token instead

servers.notes: Endpoint unchanged; the tool surface has been reshuffled rather than grown. Notion's supported-tools page now documents 24 tools, and the important change is that search has split in two: notion-search is plain keyword search over pages and people and works on a free workspace, while notion-ai-search — the one that reaches connected Slack, Drive and Jira — is a separate tool that requires Notion AI, as does notion-query-meeting-notes. Business or Enterprise is what buys the advanced filters and sorting, not search itself; the earlier note here overstated the plan wall. New since August: page-Skills tools (notion-search-skills, notion-download-skill, notion-convert-page-to-skill), notion-move-pages, notion-duplicate-page, notion-create-folder, notion-get-teams and notion-get-users. Correction that matters for scheduled agents: the hosted server is OAuth-only. Notion's own FAQ says non-interactive authorization is 'not yet' supported, and bearer tokens and PATs are not accepted over HTTP headers, so a headless nightly job cannot connect — use the local server with a NOTION_TOKEN integration token for that, accepting that Notion calls it no longer actively maintained (4.6k stars, MIT, still receiving commits — last pushed 13 Sep 2026).

servers.name: Open Edit
servers.tagline: A local editor with no GUI and no LLM: an append-only edit graph an agent drives over MCP.
servers.description: Open Edit runs as a local stdio MCP server pinned to one project directory, and hands the agent the machinery instead of the creative decisions: content-addressed ingest, word-level transcription via faster-whisper, an append-only intermediate-representation edit graph in SQLite, and melt + ffmpeg rendering. Every cut is one of 28 recorded, reversible IR operations, so a filmmaker can audit or revert what an agent did to the timeline rather than re-deriving it from a rendered file. Renders go proxy-first at 640x360 and only reach 1080p after passing a ten-check QC gate, which is the difference between an agent iterating cheaply and an agent burning an hour per bad idea.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add open-edit -- open-edit-mcp --project /ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/PROJECT

servers.notes: Two steps come before the connect command: `pip install "open-edit[mcp]"`, then `open_edit init <project-dir>` — the server refuses to start against a directory it has not initialised. The README's plain `pip install open-edit` is wrong for MCP use, because the `mcp` dependency sits in an optional extra that install skips. MIT, 46 stars, PyPI `open-edit` 1.3.1 (12 Aug 2026), repo pushed 21 Aug 2026, Python >=3.11. Six tools, not 28 — the 28 is the count of IR edit operations reachable through `edit_project`. Pinning to one project is a deliberate blast-radius limit, but it also means one registered server per cut. `run_script` executes free-form Python against the IR; it is bwrap-sandboxed on Linux and explicitly `dev`-only on Windows, so do not expose it on a Windows box you care about. Rendering needs melt (MLT) and ffmpeg on the system, and the badges claim macOS while the repo description and installers only commit to Linux and Windows — treat macOS as untested. Transcription is a separate `whisper` extra and the review UI a `serve` extra. The base package pulls in the `anthropic` SDK whether or not you use its optional built-in generation. Self-described experimental prototype with behaviour that changes between releases, a single maintainer, and legacy Remotion templates that may need a Remotion company licence; the actively maintained alternative in this space is Kinocut.

servers.name: OpusClip MCP
servers.tagline: Turns long footage into ranked short clips, then captions, edits, and schedules them.
servers.description: OpusClip's first-party hosted MCP gives an agent the whole repurposing chain: submit a file or URL, get back clips ranked by a virality score, pull the word-timed transcript, then fix a clip with named edit operations — section trims, splits, reorders, phrase cuts, filler and pause removal, caption styling, dubbing, undo. It can also report what is on screen across a source range: faces, positions, and whether the person on camera is the one speaking. From there it censors profanity, generates thumbnails and per-platform social copy, groups clips into collections, and schedules or posts them to connected accounts. For a film pipeline this is the tail end — the trailer cutdowns, the festival teasers, the vertical social pulls off a finished piece — not the edit itself. OpusClip's marketing page promises HD, 4K, or an Adobe Premiere XML project, but the MCP export tools document HD download URLs only.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http opusclip https://mcp.opus.pro/mcp
install.stdio_command: npx -y @opusclip/mcp (a launcher for the same hosted server, not a local one — npm 0.3.0, 4 Sep 2026; prefer the HTTP endpoint)

auth.key_url: OAuth in the browser on first connect — no API key; sign in at https://www.opus.pro

servers.notes: Official and hosted. The docs still say Pro-tier API access is in beta, and the editing surface has already changed underneath early adopters: editing scripts were retired, and `opusclip_get_editing_script` / `opusclip_apply_editing_script` remain only as no-op signposts that redirect to `opusclip_edit_clip`, now the only editing route. An agent holding a cached tool list from August will be calling dead names. The docs now count 27 workflow tools, including those two signposts, plus 2 thumbnail tools, while the marketing page still says 27. Trust live `tools/list` over any published count. Rechecked 27 Sep 2026: https://mcp.opus.pro/mcp still serves OAuth protected-resource metadata pointing at a WorkOS AuthKit authorization server. The docs also contradict the marketing page on export: the page advertises 4K and Premiere XML, but `opusclip_export_clip` and `opusclip_export_collection` are documented as HD download URLs only. Entitlement is not universal: the docs say Pro Beta and Max organizations get API access automatically and business customers run under their contract, so a free account may connect and find the write tools locked. Quotas are per workspace and real — 15h / 900 credits a month, a 10-credit floor charged per project regardless of length, and 4 concurrent projects, resetting on the 1st UTC. Fourteen of the tools are writes that spend credits and prompt for approval per call. The public repo is a thin 6-star wrapper (MIT, pushed 20 Sep 2026) under an org with a GitHub IP allow list, so you cannot browse its source anonymously; the docs are the real reference. Scored for short-form social, not for narrative: virality ranking and vertical reframe are the product's opinion, and it will impose it.

servers.name: OrkasVideoStudio
servers.tagline: Local MCP and CLI toolkit for agent-driven video composition, editing, analysis, and rendering.
servers.description: OrkasVideoStudio gives coding agents 37 typed MCP tools for building editable plan.json timelines, rendering HyperFrames compositions, and handling practical post work with ffmpeg. It can trim, concatenate, mix, caption, transcribe, OCR, measure loudness, detect silence and shot boundaries, and run deterministic delivery checks before a final render. The zero-key path works locally; image, speech, and video generation are optional provider-backed extensions.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add ovs -- node /absolute/path/to/Orkas-VideoStudio/packages/mcp/dist/index.js

servers.notes: Do not copy the README's install line. It advertises `npm i -g @orkas/video-studio` and `claude mcp add ovs -- npx -y @orkas/video-studio-mcp`, and neither package exists on npm — both 404 as of 10 Sep 2026, a month after the README first called publication imminent. The source build above is still the only path that works: clone, Node 22+, pnpm install && pnpm build, then point the client at packages/mcp/dist/index.js (the package's own bin target). ffmpeg and ffprobe must be on PATH for editing and local media QA. Momentum is real otherwise — 485 stars, pushed daily, last commit 10 Sep 2026, internal version 2026.9.10 — and the MCP surface has grown to 37 tools covering composition scaffolding, ffmpeg edits, loudness, OCR, silence and scene detection, plan validation and skills. The vendor also ships a native skills path (`ovs skills --install --target claude`) if you would rather not run an MCP at all. Still MIT, still local stdio only, and generated media is written to caller-supplied filesystem paths. The compose/edit/transcribe trunk needs no provider key; speech, image, and video generation require your own OpenAI, Gemini, ElevenLabs or similar credentials.

servers.name: Palmier Pro
servers.tagline: AI-native Mac timeline editor with a built-in local MCP server — closed source since v0.7.6.
servers.description: Palmier Pro is a Swift video editor built around human-agent co-editing. When the app is open, its local HTTP MCP server lets Claude, Codex, Cursor and Claude Desktop inspect the timeline, search media, add and move clips, generate media, caption, color, apply effects and export from the same project the editor is showing. It shipped as GPLv3 open source and went closed in August 2026 — the MCP surface is unchanged, the source behind it is no longer published.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http palmier-pro http://127.0.0.1:19789/mcp

auth.key_url: Requires Palmier Pro running locally with a project open; generative AI features require login/subscription or BYOK in the app

servers.notes: License change, checked 29 Aug 2026: Palmier Pro is no longer open source. The README now states that releases through v0.7.6 (Aug 19 2026) and source through the `last-gpl-source` tag were GPLv3, that later binary releases are proprietary with their source unpublished, and that the repo no longer accepts code contributions. Current release is v0.8.1 (Aug 28 2026) at 14.1k stars — still one of the fastest-moving projects in this file, but you are now trusting a binary. If a published-source editor matters to your pipeline, pin v0.7.6 or use `davinci-resolve`. Generative AI processing was always closed and needs login plus a subscription. Hard platform caveat that rules out most crews: macOS 26 (Tahoe) on Apple Silicon only — no Windows, no Linux, no Intel Macs. The MCP endpoint at 127.0.0.1:19789 is local-only and exists only while the app is running with a project open.

servers.name: PenShot (story-shot-agent)
servers.tagline: Breaks screenplays into shot lists and generates Sora/Veo/Runway-ready video prompts.
servers.description: An LLM-powered agent that parses scripts in any format, performs shot-by-shot breakdowns, and emits coherent text-to-video prompts with cross-shot character consistency. Runs as an MCP server, Python SDK, REST API, or LangGraph node — the missing link between a screenplay and a generation pipeline.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add penshot -- python -m penshot.mcp_server --max-concurrent 5 --queue-size 500 (after pip install penshot)

auth.key_url: Bring your own LLM and embedding endpoints — set PENSHOT_LLM__DEFAULT__{BASE_URL,API_KEY,MODEL_NAME} and the matching PENSHOT_EMBED__DEFAULT__* vars; OpenAI, Qwen, DeepSeek and Ollama are named as working providers

servers.notes: Still growing and genuinely active: 203 stars (up from 139 in five weeks), last commit 17 Sep 2026, PyPI 0.3.7 shipped 2 Sep 2026, MIT. Seven tools, read from the server source rather than the README — breakdown_script, get_task_status, get_task_result, cancel_task, list_tasks, get_queue_status, get_stats — and the install line now carries the --max-concurrent/--queue-size flags the project's own example config uses. THE CATCH THAT BITES: the stdio server advertises every tool with an empty JSON-Schema parameter block, so your client sees no argument names and you have to spell the arguments out in the prompt; the FastAPI surface in mcp_http_server.py has full parameter descriptions but it is a plain REST façade on :8000, not MCP over HTTP, so do not expect a remote_url. Setup is heavier than the one-line install suggests — an LLM endpoint, an embedding model and PENSHOT_REDIS_URL all have to be in .env first, or use the published ghcr.io/neopen/penshot image with docker compose. The maintainers still say it is optimized in depth for Chinese scripts with other languages 'in continuous iteration'. Async is the sane mode: submit with breakdown_script, poll get_task_status, collect get_task_result — and note task success reports as 'success', not 'completed'. Directory finding, still true: no dedicated MCP exists for Final Draft, Celtx, WriterDuet, or Fountain — script writing itself is best done with your agent directly (Fountain is plain text), stored via the Notion or Google Drive MCPs.

servers.name: PiAPI MCP Server
servers.tagline: Midjourney in an agent — plus Kling, Luma, Hailuo, Hunyuan, Wan, Suno via PiAPI.
servers.description: TypeScript MCP server over PiAPI's unified API, best known as the practical Midjourney route since Midjourney has no public API or official MCP. Also covers FLUX, Kling video and effects, Luma Dream Machine, Hailuo, Hunyuan/Skyreels/Wan video, Trellis 3D, MMAudio scoring and Suno music. Since Jul 2026 it also generates a contract-backed tool for every committed PiAPI (model, task_type) pair, so the exposed surface tracks the upstream catalog instead of only the hand-written convenience tools.

install.stdio_command: Multi-step: git clone https://github.com/apinetwork/piapi-mcp-server, npm install, npm run build, then point your client at node /absolute/path/to/dist/index.js with PIAPI_API_KEY in env. Node 16+.

auth.key_url: https://piapi.ai/workspace/key

servers.notes: MIT, 75 stars. main has not moved since the Aug 10 2026 catalog refresh. That refresh came from a drift detector that diffs PiAPI's contract, but its scheduled CI job was switched to manual-only in Jul 2026 and the sync now runs on the maintainer's own machine, so eight quiet weeks mean nobody ran it, not that nothing changed upstream. The maintainers are still working on it: an unmerged branch (codex/mcp-apps-media-preview, pushed Sep 17 2026) adds remote OAuth deployment adapters. Nothing is released from it, so there is no hosted endpoint yet. There is still no published npm package: install is clone plus npm run build, or `npx -y @smithery/cli install piapi-mcp-server --client claude`. Contract tools are named piapi_<model>_<task_type> (e.g. piapi_qubico_flux1_schnell_txt2img) alongside 23 hand-written convenience tools. Caveats: unofficial Midjourney access is a ToS gray area and only `imagine` is implemented, and long video jobs can exceed MCP client timeouts — raise them. Hosted Midjourney alternative: AceDataCloud/MidjourneyMCP.

servers.name: Pika MCP
servers.tagline: Pika's hosted media toolkit plus 20 production skills, now served from pika.art.
servers.description: Pika's official hosted MCP connects its creative suite — video, image, music, audio and voiceover generation — to Claude and other MCP clients, routing to Pika Video, Seedance 2.0, Kling, MiniMax, Veo 3, Gemini Image, ChatGPT Images and ElevenLabs among others, plus editing steps like auto captions, burned subtitles, trim, stitch and transitions. An official plugin bundle adds 20 curated skills including /podcast, /explainer, /ugc-ads, /4k-vfx, /persona-builder and /viral-hook for end-to-end short-form production.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http pika https://experiment-mcp.pika.art/api/mcp

auth.key_url: Log in to your Pika account when authorizing the connector

servers.notes: Pika moved its MCP docs off pika.me: www.pika.me/mcp still 307s to experiment.pika.art, and the documented endpoint is experiment-mcp.pika.art. The legacy mcp.pika.me/api/mcp endpoint answers 405 to a plain GET rather than 404, so it is still routed and old configs are not dead yet — but expect it to go. Pika-Labs/Pika-Plugins now carries 20 skill directories (40 stars, last pushed 20 Jul 2026), while the repo's own description still claims 3 slash commands and 42 tools at the retired mcp.pika.me host; trust the directory listing, not the blurb. The docs offer that bundle as 'npx skills add Pika-Labs/Pika-Plugins -all -y', which installs skills rather than the MCP connector. The model roster now names Sora, which OpenAI is retiring — do not build on that route. Per-tool documentation is thinner than Runway or fal.

servers.name: PixVerse MCP
servers.tagline: Official PixVerse video MCP: text/video, image animation, transitions, lip-sync and SFX.
servers.description: PixVerse's vendor-owned MCP server exposes its video-generation API through uvx for Claude, Cursor and other MCP clients. It covers text-to-video, image-to-video, video extension, two-image transitions, lip-sync, generated sound effects, and v4.5 fusion scenes, giving filmmaker agents a direct route to PixVerse's shot tools without browser automation.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add pixverse -e PIXVERSE_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY -- uvx pixverse-mcp

auth.key_url: https://platform.pixverse.ai

servers.notes: Official MIT repo, 52 stars, PyPI pixverse-mcp still 0.2.2 from 2025-10-21 with no repo push since 2025-10-22 — official but effectively frozen for eleven months as of this check, so assume the model list lags the PixVerse platform. README says Python 3.10+, but the published package metadata requires Python >=3.12; use a current uv/uvx runtime. PixVerse API credits are separate from consumer app credits.

servers.name: Plainly Videos MCP
servers.tagline: Render After Effects-backed video templates from an agent with Plainly's API.
servers.description: Plainly's official MCP server lets agents browse renderable designs and custom projects, inspect required template parameters, submit renders, and poll output status. It is a practical fit for brand-safe, repeatable film marketing assets: trailers, lower-third variants, social cutdowns, and personalized deliverables built from After Effects templates rather than free-form generation.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add plainly -e PLAINLY_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY -- npx -y @plainly-videos/mcp-server@latest

auth.key_url: https://app.plainlyvideos.com/dashboard/user/settings/general

servers.notes: Official. npm @plainly-videos/mcp-server 1.0.5 (MIT, Node >=18) was released Jan 8 2026 and is still the latest of six published versions (re-checked 10 Oct 2026). The repo (6 stars) was pushed on Sep 21 2026, but that commit only refreshed the README and added a star prompt; the last code change shipped with 1.0.5. Treat it as a shipped-and-parked vendor integration, not a living project. The README also offers a Smithery install path, which needs a Smithery key on top of the Plainly one. Four focused tools around template discovery and rendering, no prompts or resources. Templates must already exist in a paid Plainly account; the MCP renders them, it does not author them.

servers.name: Popcraft MCP
servers.tagline: Hosted OAuth MCP for 20+ video, image, audio and 3D models, with a credit preview on every call.
servers.description: Popcraft's official remote MCP puts Seedance 2.0 and 2.5, Veo 3.1, Kling 3.0 Omni, Hailuo 3, Wan 3.0, Nano Banana, GPT Image 2.5 and Seedream behind one OAuth endpoint, plus TTS, sound effects, music, 3D and Topaz upscaling. For a filmmaker-agent the useful parts are the plumbing: get_cost previews the exact credit price of any generation before it runs, models_explore returns each model's reference limits, durations and aspect ratios, and a signed-upload tool streams large reference plates from disk instead of through the context window. Results chain straight into the next call, so draft-at-480p-then-upgrade-to-1080p is one tool away.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http popcraft https://popcraft.ai/api/mcp

auth.key_url: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration — no API key; in Claude Code run /mcp → popcraft → Authenticate and sign in at https://popcraft.ai

servers.notes: New and unproven: submitted to MCP directories 29 Sep 2026, and its GitHub repo (MIT, created 25 Sep, 0 stars, 0 forks) is docs and recipes only — the server itself is closed-source. Checked 3 Oct 2026: https://popcraft.ai/api/mcp answers 401, and the Claude Code command above is the one the vendor publishes. The README lists 21 tools by name. New accounts get 100 free credits; some premium models are paid-plan only, and the agent gets a refusal it can route around. Published rates (as of 25 Sep, before plan discounts) run from 14 credits/s for Seedance 2.0 Mini to 58 credits/s for Veo 3.1 at 720p, so always pass get_cost: true first. Everything generated lands in your Popcraft web history. The Seedance 2.0 family runs a real-person check on reference media and rejects recognisable public figures before charging. The served 'skills' (ugc-ad, thumbnail-pro, h3-product-ad) are ad and social recipes, not film ones. It overlaps heavily with fal, krea and replicate, which have the longer track records. The case for Popcraft is one sign-in, no key, and per-call cost previews. Upstream sunsets hit aggregators too, so call models_explore rather than trusting a model list.

servers.name: Promptibus MCP
servers.tagline: Model intelligence MCP for prompt syntax, pricing, and budget-aware picks.
servers.description: Promptibus does not generate media; it gives agents current model profiles, pricing, parameters, prompt linting, and prompt optimization for image, video, audio, text, and code models. For filmmaker-agents spending across Runway, Sora, Veo, FLUX, Suno, Midjourney-style tools, and other fast-moving model families, it is a preflight layer that reduces stale syntax and expensive wrong-model choices.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add promptibus -- npx -y @promptibus/mcp

auth.key_url: https://promptibus.com/settings/api-keys

servers.notes: MIT, npm @promptibus/mcp 0.9.0 — still the latest of twelve releases, published May 11 2026, and neither the package nor the repo has moved since; 3 stars. The vendor page still advertises the hosted endpoint at https://promptibus.com/api/mcp alongside the npm package. Anonymous mode needs no key at 25 calls/day and 500/month across 10 free-tier models, and a free account raises that to 100/day. The staleness is the whole caveat, and the vendor's own page proves it: as of 5 Oct 2026 the free-tier list still includes Sora, whose API OpenAI scheduled for shutdown on 2026-09-24, next to Claude 4 Sonnet, GPT-4o, DALL-E 3 and Midjourney v6.1. Confirm pricing and prompt syntax at the model vendor before you spend against its advice, and do not take a Sora recommendation from it. It is a catalogue and preflight layer, not a generation router — nothing here renders a frame.

servers.name: reap MCP
servers.tagline: Hosted MCP that clips, captions, dubs, reframes, and publishes long-form footage.
servers.description: reap's official remote MCP turns a finished long cut into distribution assets without a timeline: prompt-driven moment detection pulls short clips out of a video or YouTube URL, then captions them in 100+ languages, dubs them into 80+ with voice matching, and auto-reframes to 9:16 or 1:1 with face tracking. It also carries the last mile — connected-account publishing and scheduling to YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, LinkedIn and X — which makes it the delivery end of an agent pipeline rather than another generation tool.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user reap https://mcp.reap.video/mcp

auth.key_url: One-time browser OAuth against a reap account; the endpoint serves OAuth protected-resource metadata and no API key is needed for MCP.

servers.notes: Endpoint, OAuth flow and the 29-tool surface are unchanged on re-check. The free tier still does not reach the MCP: the API reference now states flatly that 'the MCP server requires a paid plan with API access enabled', and the pricing page puts that on Creator ($9.99/mo), Studio ($29/mo) and Enterprise — so an agent connecting on a free account has nothing to call. Three of the 29 tools — publish_clip, schedule_clips, update_publisher_post — post publicly to connected social accounts, and the docs require the agent to confirm before running them; treat them as irreversible and gate them yourself. The marketing page at reap.video/mcp still contradicts the API reference, claiming '10 tools' in one place and '8 MCP Tools' in another, and listing export_video and translate_subtitles, which do not appear among the 29 documented tools; trust the API reference. That page also offers `npx add-mcp https://mcp.reap.video/mcp` as a shortcut, which is a third-party installer rather than reap's own — the claude mcp add form above is the direct route. There is no source repo, and clipping quality depends on reap's moment detection rather than anything you can tune.

servers.name: REAPER MCP
servers.tagline: Drives a live REAPER session: tracks, MIDI, FX, mixing, stems, and loudness analysis.
servers.description: The first server in this directory that puts an agent inside an actual DAW session rather than beside it. 58 tools cover project and track management, MIDI item and note writing, FX chains and parameters, sends and busses, volume and pan automation, mastering chains, and rendering to stems or a time selection. For a filmmaker-agent it closes the loop after generative SFX and dialogue: import the clips, lay them against picture, mix, then analyze loudness, dynamics and clipping before delivery.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add reaper -- reaper-mcp-server
install.stdio_command: reaper-mcp-server (after installing from source: `git clone https://github.com/bonfire-systems/reaper-mcp && pip install -e ./reaper-mcp`. The PyPI package `reaper-mcp-server` 0.1.1 predates the mcp 2.x port — see notes. Never `pip install reaper-mcp`, which is someone else's project)

auth.key_url: No key; requires a licensed REAPER install running locally with its distant API enabled

servers.notes: Install friction is the story, and it got worse. The PyPI release, `reaper-mcp-server` 0.1.1 (27 Mar 2026, still the only version since), imports `mcp.server.fastmcp` and declares an unbounded `mcp>=1.0.0`. The repo's own port commit (merged 23 Aug 2026) says mcp 2.0 removed that module, and PyPI's current mcp is 2.2.0. So a fresh `pip install reaper-mcp-server` resolves an SDK the release was not written for, and it should fail at import. Install from source, where the server now targets mcp 2.x. Pinning `mcp<2` next to the PyPI package is the untested fallback. The same port also serialises tool calls, because parallel calls under mcp 2.x interleaved on reapy's single socket. Don't confuse the names either: `reaper-mcp` on PyPI is an unrelated project by a different author (nbdy). Setup is two-stage: the server talks to REAPER through python-reapy, which needs REAPER's distant API switched on by running `scripts/enable_reapy.py` via Actions > Run ReaScript and then restarting REAPER. MIT, Python >=3.10, ~143 stars, classified Alpha on PyPI. The repo was last pushed 23 Aug 2026 after two quiet months: alive, but not busy. REAPER itself is a paid licence after its evaluation period, and pulls in librosa, numpy and soundfile for the analysis tools.

servers.name: Recraft MCP Server
servers.tagline: Official hosted Recraft server: raster + vector generation, styles, upscale, backgrounds.
servers.description: Recraft's official MCP is now a hosted, OAuth-gated endpoint covering text-to-image, image-to-image and variations in raster and SVG, region editing and object removal, custom style creation, vectorization, background removal and replacement, and upscaling. Uniquely useful for film work needing brand-consistent styles, title and poster art, and clean vector assets. The old local npm package is dead — connect over HTTP instead.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http recraft https://mcp.recraft.ai/mcp

auth.key_url: OAuth in the browser on first connect; no API key to manage. Needs a Recraft account at recraft.ai

servers.notes: Re-checked 8 Oct 2026: endpoint, OAuth flow and the documented Claude Code and mcp-remote commands are unchanged. The stdio entry is not a local server — it is the mcp-remote bridge Recraft's own docs print for clients that cannot speak streamable HTTP, pointed at the same hosted endpoint. The local package @recraft-ai/mcp-recraft-server (last v1.6.5) is deprecated and its repo is archived; the repo link is kept only for history. Billing: the hosted server deducts from your Recraft plan credits, the same balance Recraft Studio spends, at per-operation rates listed under Plans and billing — free accounts get a small allowance. In Claude Code on the web, generated images may fail to download unless img.recraft.ai is added to the environment's allowed network domains. tools_sample is null because Recraft's docs describe capabilities rather than tool names and the endpoint is OAuth-gated, so the list cannot be enumerated without an account.

servers.name: ReelsFarm MCP
servers.tagline: Hosted short-form studio for AI avatars, product scenes, UGC videos, and social delivery.
servers.description: ReelsFarm is a hosted short-form content studio for agent-driven production: one MCP connection covers AI avatar generation, product scenes, UGC videos, slideshows, asset libraries, and social delivery. For short-form filmmakers and ad teams, creation, scheduling, and publishing share one authenticated workflow instead of separate model endpoints.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http reelsfarm https://mcp.reelsfarm.com/mcp

auth.key_url: https://reelsfarm.com/docs/mcp — sign in with a ReelsFarm account and authorize the MCP client, or paste an rfmcp_ API key from the account MCP tab as an Authorization: Bearer header

servers.name: RunAPI MCP Server
servers.tagline: Browse, price, and run 130+ image, video, audio and voice models through one MCP.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add runapi -s user -- npx -y @runapi.ai/mcp

auth.key_url: https://runapi.ai/mcp (hosted remote takes OAuth or an API key as bearer; the local package adds a browser `login` tool that writes ~/.config/runapi/config.json)

servers.name: Sanzaru (OpenAI audio MCP)

auth.key_url: https://platform.openai.com (API keys)

servers.name: Silhouette MCP Server
servers.tagline: The only roto, paint, and planar-tracking MCP — Boris FX Silhouette driven by an agent.

Two modes via SFX_MCP_MODE: 'online' (default) drives a running instance over its RPC socket with live UI updates and grouped undo blocks; 'offline' runs Silhouette headless per tool call for batch, CI, and farm work — Configure Client always writes online, so offline needs a hand edit. Configure Client for Claude Code shells out to `claude mcp remove silhouette --scope user` then `claude mcp add`, so re-running it is safe. execute_script is an unguarded escape hatch that runs arbitrary fx Python. Not cheap and not standalone-free: $545/yr or $103/mo when last quoted in Aug 2026 — the Boris FX store renders prices client-side and could not be re-read here, so treat the figures as indicative. servers.name: Sonicmatch
servers.tagline: Watches the footage, then returns license-safe music, a hook window, and a ducking spec.
servers.description: Sonicmatch is music supervision shaped for an agent: ingest a cut, analyse mood, energy curve, speech coverage and scene cuts, then get back a ranked shortlist of tracks with the license printed on every row, a 12–20 second hook in/out, an ffmpeg ducking recipe, and a beat-snapped cut list. It reads the picture rather than the script, which is the difference between a music search and a music choice. The intended production use is pointing it at an Artlist or Epidemic library you already pay for, via a JSON manifest, so the scoring logic runs over a catalogue you are actually cleared to deliver.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add sonicmatch -- uvx --from git+https://github.com/js713-lab/sonic-match-mcp.git sonicmatch-mcp
install.stdio_command: uvx --from git+https://github.com/js713-lab/sonic-match-mcp.git sonicmatch-mcp — or pip install git+https://github.com/js713-lab/sonic-match-mcp.git then run sonicmatch-mcp. Needs Python 3.10+ and ffmpeg/ffprobe on PATH; add --http --port 8765 for Streamable HTTP instead of stdio.

auth.key_url: No key required. Optional: GEMINI_API_KEY for video understanding, JAMENDO_CLIENT_ID and FREESOUND_API_KEY for extra catalogues, SONICMATCH_LIBRARY_PATH / EPIDEMIC_LIBRARY_PATH / ARTLIST_LIBRARY_PATH for a library you already licensed

servers.notes: Young and thin, listed for the shape of the idea rather than the catalogue behind it. Checked 23 Sep 2026: MIT, first public release 10 Sep 2026, one v0.2.0 tag, last commit 16 Sep, a single maintainer, 94 stars against zero forks — and published to the official MCP registry as io.github.js713-lab/sonicmatch-mcp with an .mcpb bundle. Not on PyPI, so every install path is a git checkout; the twelve tools above were read off the source, not just the README. The built-in catalogue is 22 seed tracks whose preview and download URLs are null on purpose, so out of the box recommend_bgm hands you rows you cannot fetch and preview_mix synthesises a demo bed instead of real music — the useful configuration is your own licensed Artlist or Epidemic manifest, or the optional Jamendo and Freesound keys. Platform URL ingest via yt-dlp ships off by default for ToS reasons; leave it off and feed it local files. The licensing discipline is the best thing here — non-commercial tracks are never auto-recommended and generated beds are excluded from recommendations — but a CC label is not a Content ID waiver, and CC-BY still needs attribution in your credits. For a cleared catalogue with the rights already settled, the Epidemic Sound entry is the grown-up option; Sonicmatch is the analysis layer you would put in front of it.

servers.name: Sonilo MCP
servers.tagline: Score and effects generated against the cut, from a catalogue trained on licensed music.
servers.description: Sonilo's official MCP server scores picture rather than prompts: video_to_music watches a clip and composes to its pacing and cut points, video_to_sfx lays effects against the same timing, and the video_to_video_* variants hand back the muxed file instead of a loose stem. Text-only tools cover fixed-length cues, plus dubbing and audio ducking under dialogue. The reason a filmmaker-agent should care is provenance: Sonilo says its models are trained exclusively on professionally licensed music including Shutterstock's catalogue, which is the claim no Suno wrapper can make.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add sonilo -- uvx sonilo-mcp

auth.key_url: https://platform.sonilo.com/dashboard/api-keys

servers.notes: MIT, Python >=3.10, PyPI sonilo-mcp 0.27.0 shipped 19 Sep 2026 — 47 releases since mid-July, so it is the fastest-moving music server in this directory, at 53 stars and listed in the official MCP registry. The roster keeps growing: video_to_sound and video_to_video_sound (music plus effects in one pass), video_to_video_sfx and a proofread tool for dubbing scripts have joined the tools sampled here. Set SONILO_API_KEY or run `sonilo login` from the sonilo-cli npm package first; the server has no hosted remote. Read the licensing page before you deliver: commercial-use rights are plan-gated to Pro, Premium, Enterprise and 'eligible API users' — Free and Creator output is personal use only — and Sonilo states plainly that those rights 'do not remove every copyright, platform, client, or broadcast review'. The training-data claim is Sonilo's, not independently audited. Hard limits per the current README: video-to-music up to 360s, video-to-SFX up to 480s, dubbing up to 300s, uploads typically 300 MB; output lands in ~/Desktop unless SONILO_MCP_BASE_PATH is set, and TIME_OUT_SECONDS defaults to 600. Inputs: H.264/HEVC/VP9/AV1 in mp4/mov/m4v/webm. Billing is per second generated with a couple of free runs per tool, except dubbing, which bills from the first call.

servers.tagline: Remote MCP for searching and licensing restored 8mm and Super 8 home-movie footage.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http stockfilm https://api.stockfilm.com/mcp

The 217,000+ clip figure the server advertised in August is gone from serverInfo and from every tool description; the site now says 162,000+ clips across 121 countries and 900+ cities, 1930s–1980s. Scope is narrow by design — amateur home movies only, no news, sport or studio material; for those see getty-images in this directory. The second hostname, https://mcp.stockfilm.com/mcp, still answers identically; the vendor's own docs point at api.stockfilm.com, used above.

servers.name: studio-state
servers.tagline: Keeps AI-film characters, locations, shots, and lock status grounded in project files.

Its tools orient the session, report per-shot status, and write only a small sidecar when a shot is fired, locked, or needs rework.

auth.key_url: Requires a local project folder containing _pipeline/STATE.json and episodes/

servers.notes: MIT, still live but frozen: re-checked 20 Sep 2026 and the last push is unchanged at 16 Jun 2026 — three months without a commit — with still 0 stars, so treat it as one studio's shim published rather than a maintained project. The repo is not archived and INSTALL.md is still in place, so nothing has broken; nothing has moved either. Prerequisites the README front-loads: Python 3.9+ and `pip install "mcp[cli]"`, plus a project root containing _pipeline/STATE.json and episodes/ — run tests/test_acceptance.py against the bundled demo project first (expect 4/4). It is a state shim, not a generator, and the paid Studio Method pack is upsold in the README. The useful bit is safe by design — only `update_shot` writes, and only to a per-scene `shot_status.json` sidecar.

servers.name: SunoMCP (AceDataCloud)
servers.tagline: Full Suno workflow via a third-party API: songs, lyrics, stems, extends, personas.
servers.description: The most complete Suno bridge available as an MCP server, built on AceDataCloud's reseller API: generate songs from prompts or custom lyrics, extend, cover, remaster, mash up, replace a time range, split stems, and export WAV, MIDI or MP4. Personas keep one vocalist consistent across cues. It reaches capabilities Suno itself exposes through no official API or MCP — which is precisely the problem.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add suno --transport http https://suno.mcp.acedata.cloud/mcp -h "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN"

auth.key_url: https://platform.acedata.cloud

servers.notes: Suno still has NO official public API as of late September 2026 — its CPO posted an intake form in July 2026 saying the company is only exploring a developer API, partner-curated, with no public endpoints, docs or date. So this and every other Suno wrapper is an unofficial reseller, plausibly against Suno's ToS, and no commercial-rights claim on the output can be guaranteed. Same for all Udio wrappers. For music you can actually clear, prefer Sonilo, Lyria (Google GenMedia) or Stable Audio via the fal hub. Mechanically it is alive and moving: PyPI mcp-suno 2026.9.9.0 shipped 9 Sep 2026 — the same day Suno launched its v6 family — adding chirp-v6, chirp-v6-wild and chirp-v6-mini, plus new custom-model tools; MIT, 55 stars, roughly 35–40 suno_-prefixed tools. Trap: SUNO_DEFAULT_MODEL still defaults to chirp-v5-5 in both README and source, so set it to a v6 id explicitly if you want the current model, and call suno_list_models rather than trusting any list. SUNO_REQUEST_TIMEOUT is 1800s, because renders are slow. The older unprefixed tool names in the lower half of the README are out of date.

servers.name: Sync MCP Server
servers.tagline: Official Sync MCP for lipsync generation, voice cloning, and TTS on existing footage.
servers.description: Sync's own MCP server wraps the sync.so API: take a video plus an audio track and regenerate the performer's mouth to match, with cost estimation before you spend, asset and project management, voice cloning, and TTS. Unlike avatar platforms that synthesize a presenter, this retimes lips on footage you already shot — the practical tool for dub passes, ADR fixes, and localized versions that keep the original take. Tools are generated from the Sync OpenAPI spec at startup, so new endpoints appear without a server update.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add sync -- npx -y @sync.so/mcp-server --api-key YOUR_API_KEY

auth.key_url: https://sync.so/settings/api-keys

servers.notes: Official and MIT, and every install field above re-checked unchanged: the hosted endpoint takes OAuth in Claude web (no key needed), while stdio needs SYNC_API_KEY — or omit it and the server runs a device-auth flow, caching a token at ~/.config/sync/mcp-credentials.json. Node 18+. Pricing is the same on re-check — $5/month Hobbyist through $249/month Scale, per-second generation charges of roughly $0.04–0.05 on every tier, and caps on clip length (1 min at the bottom, 30 min at the top), concurrent jobs and voice clones — so call generate_estimate-cost before long renders; the pricing page pitches a free trial but lists no free plan. Models named there are still Lipsync-2-Pro, Sync-3 and React-1; ask models_get rather than assuming. Watch the surface mismatch: the repo README documents voices, tts and projects tools, but Sync's public API reference only covers generations, assets, models, estimate, batch and healthcheck — tools are generated from the live OpenAPI spec at startup, so read tools/list instead of trusting either list. The repo woke up (last pushed 7 Sep 2026, adding session and upload limits to the HTTP transport) but is still a 1-star project, and npm @sync.so/mcp-server sits at 0.1.4 from 16 Mar 2026 — tolerable only because the tool surface comes from the spec, not the package. Ethics and rights: relighting someone's mouth to say new words needs the performer's consent, and many jurisdictions and union agreements now require it explicitly.

servers.name: Tavus MCP
servers.tagline: Phoenix replicas, persona videos, lipsync, and conversational AI via the Tavus API.
servers.description: Comprehensive community MCP server exposing 25 tools across the full Tavus API: Phoenix replica (digital twin) training, persona management, video generation, real-time conversational video (CVI), lipsync, and speech synthesis.
