install.stdio_command: Build from source: clone rakeshdavid/Tavus-MCP, npm install && npm run build, then run node build/index.js with TAVUS_API_KEY. Smithery is the documented alternative: npx -y @smithery/cli install @rakeshdavid/tavus-mcp --client claude

auth.key_url: https://platform.tavus.io

servers.notes: The landscape changed on 2026-08-31 and the answer did not. Tavus now has an official MCP — hosted at https://mcp.tavus.io/mcp (`claude mcp add -s user --transport http tavus https://mcp.tavus.io/mcp`, browser OAuth, no key in your config) or locally via `uvx --from 'tavus-cli[daily]' tavus-mcp` from PyPI tavus-cli 0.4.3. It is not a substitute: all 72 of its tools configure PALs — prompts, objectives, guardrails, knowledge, tool wiring, chat-mode testing — and Tavus's own tools reference lists no replica training, no video generation and no lipsync. That is a conversational-agent product, which is why it is not listed here separately and this server still is. What you are living with, re-confirmed 2026-09-09: the README's npm package (tavus-mcp) is still not on npm — the registry 404s — so install from source or via Smithery; the repo has had no commit since 2025-07-09 and holds 2 stars, so treat it as unmaintained rather than quiet; it is built on an old MCP SDK version. Tavus free developer plan: ~25 min conversational video + 5 min generation.

servers.name: Topaz Labs MCP
servers.tagline: Official Topaz Labs MCP — enhance and upscale images with Topaz AI models.
servers.description: Topaz Labs' own MCP server: send an image path or URL, get back an enhanced/upscaled version from one of 8 Topaz models — four standard (Standard V2, Low Resolution V2, CGI, High Fidelity V2) and four generative (Redefine, Recover 3, Standard MAX, Wonder 2) — defaulting to Standard V2 with auto-upscale to 2K. The official path to Topaz-grade enhancement for stills, plates, and frames in an agent pipeline.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add topaz -e TOPAZ_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY -- npx -y @topazlabs/mcp

auth.key_url: https://developer.topazlabs.com/getting-started/api-key-setup

servers.notes: Official, MIT, TypeScript — and dormant: re-checked 18 Sep 2026 and nothing has moved. v0.1.14 on npm and the last repo commit both still date to 16 Feb 2026, seven months ago; the repo has gained one star in five weeks (6 total) and no commits. It installs and runs, but nobody is extending it. IMAGE ONLY — the README still says 'Image only -- video enhancement is not yet supported' via MCP even though Topaz's developer API covers Video AI, Photo AI, and Gigapixel, and it still lists HTTP streaming transport as 'not yet supported but may be added in a future release', so ChatGPT, remote agents and web/mobile clients are out. One tool, image-enhance, taking a local path or URL: a filesystem-capable client is required (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code — not Claude's browser chat). The key_url here changed this run — Topaz's old how-do-i-get-my-api-key page now 404s and the live page is getting-started/api-key-setup, which warns the key is shown exactly once at creation. For Topaz VIDEO upscaling today, go around it to the Topaz models hosted on fal.ai via the fal MCP (fal-ai/topaz/upscale/video — re-confirmed 18 Sep 2026 at $0.01/second up to 720p, $0.02 to 1080p, $0.08 above 1080p, doubled for 60fps output and halved for Gaia 2).

servers.name: Tripo MCP
servers.tagline: Official Tripo MCP — text-to-3D assets generated and imported into Blender.
servers.description: VAST's official MCP server generates 3D assets from natural language via the Tripo API and imports them into Blender through the Tripo Blender addon. Quick path from prompt to set-dressing props and previz geometry, if you already live in Blender.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add tripo -- uvx tripo-mcp

auth.key_url: https://platform.tripo3d.ai

servers.notes: Official and now 197 stars, but abandoned in practice: re-checked 3 Sep 2026 and nothing has moved since the last review — README still says alpha, PyPI tripo-mcp is still 0.1.2 from Apr 12 2025, and the repo has had no push since Apr 14 2025, sixteen and a half months. Not archived, so it still reads as live; treat the stars as history, not health. Still scoped to Blender-addon integration and requires the separate Tripo AI Blender Addon plus a running Blender. The multi-provider alternative mordor-forge/trident-mcp (Tripo + Meshy + Rodin) was last pushed Jul 9 2026 and is fresher, but tiny at 6 stars — evaluate before you depend on it. Meshy's server is the better-maintained official option in this niche.

servers.name: TwelveLabs Jockey
servers.tagline: Cross-video agent MCP: build a knowledge store, then ask your whole library questions.
servers.description: Jockey is TwelveLabs' agentic layer over a corpus rather than a clip. You create a knowledge store, add video and images to it, and then ask questions that span the whole collection — Jockey decomposes the query, retrieves, segments and reasons across items, and answers with clip citations rather than a wall of prose. For an editor this is the archive researcher: find every shot of a location across three seasons of footage, track a face or object through unrelated rushes, or have it assemble a highlight lane before anyone opens the NLE. It is a hosted OAuth endpoint, so there is nothing to install and no key to manage.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user jockey https://mcp.twelvelabs.io/jockey/mcp

auth.key_url: Browser OAuth against a TwelveLabs account — free signup at https://playground.twelvelabs.io

servers.notes: Still a research preview: the Jockey product page says it is "currently accepting limited sign-ups", so a free account is not a guaranteed seat. Pricing is now published there, metered by knowledge-store size: Free at 5 GB, Plus at $20/month for 100 GB, Pro at $100/month for 500 GB, with rate limits rising by tier. A real season of rushes outgrows the free tier quickly. Tool names are null because TwelveLabs does not publish a catalogue — the docs tell you to ask the connected client to list them, so run `tools/list` and see what you get rather than trusting any third-party listing. Hard limits are 4 GB per video and 32 MB per image, video URLs must be publicly reachable, and ingestion is asynchronous: adding a corpus is a wait, not a call. OAuth sessions can expire, and the docs tell you to re-authenticate through `/mcp` when that happens. Clients without widget support get a text fallback instead of the gallery/timeline/highlight-reel UI, which in practice means the citations are still usable but the assembly view is not. Requires a client that supports remote HTTP servers with OAuth. The docs name Claude and Claude Code, and the product page says ChatGPT support is "coming soon". Re-checked 10 Oct 2026: the endpoint and install command are unchanged. Do not confuse this with the single-video `twelvelabs` entry, which is a separate server on a separate host with an API key.

servers.name: TwelveLabs MCP
servers.tagline: Index, search, and analyze video libraries with Pegasus and Marengo through MCP.
servers.description: TwelveLabs' MCP server gives agents semantic video search and analysis: create indexes, upload or batch-index clips, search by natural language or image, summarize footage, generate chapters/highlights, and retrieve embeddings. For filmmakers this is the missing dailies-and-library brain — ask for the shot where a character enters frame, find matching B-roll, or produce structured notes from long generated cuts.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add twelvelabs -e TWELVELABS_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY -- npx -y --package=twelvelabs-mcp twelvelabs-mcp-stdio

auth.key_url: https://playground.twelvelabs.io

TwelveLabs' docs have moved the hosted copy of them off mcp.twelvelabs.io to mcp-alpic.twelvelabs.io — if you connected a hosted URL before roughly mid-2026, it is stale — and mcp.twelvelabs.io now serves the cross-video Jockey server instead (listed separately as `twelvelabs-jockey`). The docs name only the new host, not a full endpoint path, so `remote_url` stays null here; the stdio install below is the path that is actually documented end to end. npm twelvelabs-mcp is still 1.0.0, published May 12 2026 and untouched since (re-checked 9 Oct 2026) — five months without a release while TwelveLabs' docs now lead with Jockey only, so treat this tool list as frozen. Maintained by the `twelvelabs` npm account plus Teraflop; the linked repo is the JS SDK (18 stars, pushed Oct 7 2026), not the MCP server — no MCP source exists anywhere in the twelvelabs-io org, so there is nothing to read for the server itself. The stdio bin is `twelvelabs-mcp-stdio`; the explicit `--package=twelvelabs-mcp` npx form avoids npm confusing the package name with the bin name. Local file and folder uploads only work over stdio; hosted HTTP expects API-key headers and public/direct video URLs. For new setups, start with Jockey unless you specifically need per-video embeddings or index-level control.

The reason to reach for it over Epic's first-party server is engine coverage — UE 5.5 through 5.7 — and Blueprint authoring depth.

auth.key_url: https://flopperam.com/account (hosted mode); local mode is free but requires compiling the bundled UnrealMCP C++ plugin

The README's licence line says MIT but the repo contains no LICENCE file and GitHub's licence API returns 404, so the grant is unconfirmed. The hosted endpoint still answers 401 unauthenticated, so it is alive and key-gated; Aura's own product page markets an editor/Claude Code agent for Unreal 5.4+ without mentioning MCP, which is the direction the funding is going. Landscape: Epic now ships a first-party server for UE 5.8 (unreal-mcp-epic); chongdashu/unreal-mcp is still the most-starred at 2.1k but has not been pushed since Apr 2025; ChiR24/Unreal_mcp (853 stars, MIT, pushed Aug 29 2026, TypeScript + a C++ Automation Bridge plugin) is the most actively maintained community option.

servers.name: Unreal MCP (Epic Games)
servers.tagline: Epic's first-party in-editor MCP server for Unreal Engine 5.8.
servers.description: Ships inside the Unreal Editor as the ModelContextProtocol plugin, exposing toolsets that spawn actors, configure lighting, create material instances, inspect widgets, and run automation tests. Discovery is indirect — three meta-tools (list_toolsets, describe_toolset, call_tool) walk a registry of UToolsetDefinition-derived toolsets, so studios can register their own. For virtual production and previz this is the version that will not rot when the engine moves.

install.claude_code: Enable the Unreal MCP and All Toolsets plugins in Edit > Plugins, start the server (Editor Preferences > General > Model Context Protocol > Auto Start Server, or the console command ModelContextProtocol.StartServer), then run ModelContextProtocol.GenerateClientConfig ClaudeCode to write .mcp.json in the project root and launch your agent from there.

auth.key_url: No auth. Requires Unreal Engine 5.8 with the ModelContextProtocol and AllToolsets plugins enabled (Toolset Registry is pulled in as a dependency)

servers.notes: Marked Experimental by Epic: 'use caution when shipping with it', APIs and data formats subject to change, many features incomplete. HTTP and Server-Sent Events only — stdio and WebSocket transports are not supported, so remote-agent setups need their own tunnel. It binds loopback at http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp (port and path configurable), and Epic states plainly that the server 'only accepts connections from the same machine, has no authentication layer, and is not designed for remote use' — anything that reaches that port drives your editor. ModelContextProtocol.StopServer and .RefreshTools complete the console surface. UE 5.8 only; on 5.5-5.7 or for hosted use, see the unreal-engine entry.

servers.name: Valossa Video Assistant MCP
servers.tagline: Hosted video-understanding MCP: transcripts, shots, visual scenes, soundbites, and clips.
servers.description: Valossa's official remote MCP hands an agent a watched-and-indexed copy of your footage: speech transcripts, shot and visual-scene breakdowns, overviews, summaries and highlights, natural-language questions about what is on screen, and clip export that comes back as a download URL. For an assistant editor it is the logging pass — find the take, find the soundbite, pull the selects — run against material Valossa has already analysed instead of against raw files. Uploads are a two-step prepare-then-commit handshake, and get_quota_status exists because everything interesting here costs quota.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http valossa https://mcp-assistant.valossa.com/mcp

auth.key_url: Browser OAuth against a Valossa Assistant account created at https://assistant.valossa.com/signup — no API key

servers.notes: There is no free tier, only a 7-day trial: 30 analysis minutes, 100 task credits, no card, and a 15-minute cap per video while trialling. After that it is a EUR 29 credit pack or monthly plans from EUR 14.90. Two meters run at once — imports burn analysis minutes, exports and agent questions burn task credits — so check get_quota_status before turning an agent loose on a feature-length rush. Hard ceilings are 7 GB and 5 hours per file. It analyses, it does not edit: clips arrive as download URLs, and there is no NLE round-trip, no EDL, no timeline. Closest comparison is the TwelveLabs entry; the reason to pick this one is jurisdiction — Valossa is Finnish and states that video stays in the EU and is not used to train models. Registered in the official MCP Registry as com.valossa/video-assistant-mcp (v1.0.0, published 2026-06-25). No public source repo, so the documentation page is the only reference, and roughly half the 23 documented tools write data or spend quota. Re-checked 7 Oct 2026: endpoint, OAuth flow, 23-tool split, 7 GB / 5 h limits, trial terms and EUR pricing all unchanged; the MCP Registry was unreachable that day, so the registry line above is from the previous check.

The MCP server exposes 11 tools; the README's install is clone-and-pip, nothing is on PyPI. A separate TypeScript wrapper in the repo's mcp-server/ folder talks to the HTTP API on port 9001, but its npm package is marked 'once published', so use the Python stdio server. Drafts target CapCut International or Jianying and still have to land in the app's drafts folder; draft formats change with app updates, so test against your installed version. VectCut also runs a hosted cloud editor at vectcut.com with preview and cloud render — its pricing and any hosted MCP endpoint were not verified here. ByteDance offers no official CapCut MCP. servers.tagline: VEED's hosted MCP for talking-head video: pick a character, pick a voice, send a script.

servers.name: VibeFrame

The documented keys are OPENAI_API_KEY, FAL_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, RUNWAY_API_SECRET and KLING_API_KEY. MIT, npm @vibeframe/mcp-server still 0.115.2 (Jul 26 2026, Node >=20, bin `vibeframe-mcp`); the repo is 165 stars and was last pushed the same day, so the fast release cadence noted in June has been five weeks of silence — pin a version anyway, but check the repo before you build on it. Claude Desktop users can skip npx entirely — the repo ships a vibeframe.mcpb extension bundle on its latest release. The hosted Video Jungle service is still up and its site advertises 6 free generated videos before usage depends on the account, but nobody is maintaining the client. servers.tagline: Script, voiceover or storyboard to finished video, plus clip, image, music and avatar generation.

auth.key_url: https://app.videogen.io/api (keys start sk_videogen_live_)

servers.name: Vimeo MCP Server
servers.tagline: Official Vimeo remote MCP: library search, analytics, retention, and metadata editing.
servers.description: Vimeo's official remote MCP server, now in public beta, connects an agent to your Vimeo library over OAuth. It searches videos across accounts and teams, reads transcripts, chapters, comments and text tracks, pulls performance metrics including geographic data and viewer retention, edits metadata and privacy, manages showcases, and can even create editing sessions and render videos programmatically. For a delivery pipeline it is the honest post-publish feedback loop: what actually held an audience, shot by shot.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http vimeo https://mcp.vimeo.com/mcp

auth.key_url: OAuth against your Vimeo account; the server advertises https://mcp.vimeo.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and no token is configured by hand

servers.notes: Public beta as of the current docs, upgraded from the private beta announced at REFRAME in Oct 2025 — Vimeo says all of it is subject to change without notice. Endpoint is https://mcp.vimeo.com/mcp; https://mcp.vimeo.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource still answers (re-checked 2026-10-01), names mcp.vimeo.com as its own authorization server, accepts the bearer in the header only, and advertises six scopes — public, private, stats, upload, edit, create. Read that list before you consent: the write surface is genuine, and the scopes you grant decide how much of your library an agent can change. ChatGPT clients use https://mcp.vimeo.com/sse instead, same tools. Destructive actions such as deleting videos are deliberately excluded. Vimeo recommends Pro or above because API rate limits scale with plan, so expect a thin experience on free. The docs page is still a client-rendered SPA and invisible to crawlers (re-checked 2026-10-01), so tool names remain unpublished.

servers.name: Vivideo MCP
servers.tagline: Hosted MCP over a multi-model video roster, with avatars, voices, and brand kits.
servers.description: Vivideo's official MCP server fronts its generation API with thirteen tools: an auto mode that turns a brief into a finished video, a manual mode for shot-level control, and roster lookups for models, avatars, voices and brand kits. estimate_credits prices a job before you spend, and get_video/wait_for_video/list_videos handle the polling an agent would otherwise hand-roll. Useful when you want one connection covering generation plus voiceover, captions and brand-consistent assembly rather than wiring three servers together.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http vivideo https://api.vivideo.ai/mcp -h "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"

auth.key_url: https://app.vivideo.ai/account/api-keys

servers.notes: Listed in the official MCP registry with both the npm package and the hosted remote, and the endpoint still answers 405 to a GET on 26 Sep 2026 — correct behaviour for a POST-only streamable HTTP server. The docs match this entry: the same thirteen tools, the same `claude mcp add --transport http` command with a vv_live_-prefixed Bearer key, and VIVIDEO_API_KEY for the npx route. Everything else is vendor-stated: the package is closed source with no public repo, so you cannot audit what the wrapper sends, and @vivideo/mcp has sat at 1.0.2 since 28 Jul 2026 while the API around it moves. The homepage still leads with 'Powered by Sora 2' and lists Sora 2 Pro two days after OpenAI's announced 24 Sep 2026 API removal — treat the published roster as stale marketing and call list_models before you plan a shoot around any model. The free tier's 'unlimited', watermark-free generation with commercial rights is homepage copy we could not verify against machine-readable terms; read the plan before delivering client work.

servers.name: Wireflow
servers.tagline: Exposes whole ad-creative workflows over MCP rather than individual model endpoints.
servers.description: Wireflow is a hosted ad-creative platform that fans a single brief out into hundreds of static, carousel, video and UGC variants, with brand kits, compositing, colour grading and publishing to social. Its MCP connector exposes the workflow layer rather than raw models: an agent searches recipes, clones a template or authors a workflow from a prompt, runs it, polls the execution and schedules automations. Since the August check the connector has grown a timeline surface — read the cut, edit it, preview frames — so an agent can inspect and adjust the assembled video rather than only trigger a render. For a filmmaker-agent, that means one call produces a finished, brand-consistent deliverable instead of a shot you still have to assemble.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http wireflow https://www.wireflow.ai/api/mcp

auth.key_url: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591) — sign in with a Wireflow account, no pre-shared credentials

servers.notes: Disclosure: a direct competitor to Martini, this directory's sponsor, listed on the same terms as everything else. Endpoint verified alive and auth-gated (401) on 2026-09-08 and the tool list is taken verbatim from Wireflow's own MCP docs, which now claim 43 registered tools while naming 25 — trust live `tools/list` over either figure. Closed source, no public repo, and the vendor documents only connector-UI setup — the CLI command above is the standard streamable-HTTP form of the documented endpoint. Credits are the real constraint: the free tier browses and builds but has no generation credits, Starter is $24/month for 1,600, Professional $45 for 4,300, Team $249 for 21,500, with $10 top-ups buying 500-600 more depending on tier. Budget roughly 30 credits per image and 17 credits per second of video, so a minute of video is not cheap. Useful nuance the docs are explicit about: only run_workflow and automation execution spend credits, so authoring and cloning workflows costs nothing until you ask for a render. Ad-format oriented; it is not a general shot-generation tool.

servers.name: Wistia MCP Server
servers.tagline: Official Wistia remote MCP: upload, trim, caption, dub, publish, and read the analytics.
servers.description: Wistia's official hosted MCP puts a whole video library behind an agent: upload or import media, trim and swap versions, order captions, translations, dubs and extended audio descriptions, drive the Remix AI editor, organise folders, tags and channels, then read engagement and visitor analytics back out. For a film team it is the delivery-and-measurement end — festival reels, behind-the-scenes cuts, press kits and webinars hosted somewhere you can see who actually watched, and for how long. A ?toolsets= query parameter on the endpoint narrows the surface to media, analytics, captions, remix or nine other groups instead of exposing everything at once.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http wistia https://api.wistia.com/mcp/api

auth.key_url: Browser OAuth against a Wistia account, or an access token sent as an Authorization: Bearer header; either way the seat must be Owner or Manager

servers.notes: Launched 2026-07-22 and free to use on any plan, including the $0 tier (25 GB, one seat) — but role-gated: only Owners and Managers can connect an agent, so a shared editor seat gets nothing. Wistia does not publish individual tool names, only the twelve toolsets, and by default the endpoint exposes every tool it has; pin ?toolsets=media,analytics or similar unless you want the agent paging through the full API. The write surface is a live public library — archive, swap, trim, bulk update and channel publishing are all reachable and some are irreversible, so gate them yourself. Remix and dubbing spend an AI credit balance that the account toolset reports. There is no source repo and the docs are the only reference, and Wistia's own guidance is to ask the agent what it can do because the surface is still expanding. Scope check: this is marketing and B2B video hosting, not a screener or festival delivery platform — no DCP, no watermarked screener workflow. For those, see the Frame.io and Vimeo entries. Re-checked 7 Oct 2026: endpoint, Claude Code command, OAuth-or-token auth, Owner/Manager restriction and the twelve toolsets all unchanged in the docs.

servers.name: YouTube MCP Server (data)
servers.tagline: Token-optimized YouTube Data API server for video, channel, and trend analytics.
servers.description: A high-efficiency MCP server returning structured, token-minimized data from the YouTube Data API v3 (claims up to 87% token reduction vs raw API). Covers video details, search, transcripts, channel statistics, trending, and outlier-channel discovery — the research side of distribution: study what works before you publish.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add youtube -e YOUTUBE_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY -- npx -y @kirbah/mcp-youtube

auth.key_url: Google Cloud Console → enable YouTube Data API v3 → Credentials → API key. Transcript-only use runs with no key at all.

servers.notes: MIT, npm v1.1.14 released 2026-09-11; that release raised the floor to Node 22+, and everything since has been Dependabot bumps (repo pushed 2026-10-01), so it is maintained rather than developed. Still only 29 stars. Read-only: no upload, so pair it with yutu. Quota reality: searchVideos costs 100 units per call and getChannelTopVideos 101 against a 10k/day default, and getVideoComments is 1 unit plus another per top-level comment once you ask for replies. The 'zero API cost' transcripts do not use the Data API at all — they go through youtube-transcript-plus, which scrapes YouTube's timedtext endpoint, so treat transcript pulls as a ToS gray area and expect them to break when YouTube changes it. MongoDB is less optional than it looks: MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING is required for findConsistentOutlierChannels and the README recommends it for caching everything else. Higher-profile alternative: ZubeidHendricks/youtube-mcp-server (577 stars, but no push since 2026-08-08, multi-key quota fallback).

servers.name: yutu (YouTube MCP + CLI)
servers.tagline: Automate your whole YouTube channel — including real video uploads — via OAuth.
servers.description: A Go-based CLI, MCP server, and agent toolkit for YouTube that automates the full workflow: uploading videos, editing metadata, managing playlists, comments, captions, and thumbnails. Still the only well-maintained MCP option that does real YouTube uploads via OAuth — Google ships no official YouTube MCP as of August 2026.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add -e YUTU_CREDENTIAL=/absolute/path/to/client_secret.json -e YUTU_CACHE_TOKEN=/absolute/path/to/youtube.token.json yutu -- yutu mcp

auth.key_url: Google Cloud Console: enable YouTube Data API v3, create a Desktop-app OAuth client, save client_secret.json, then run yutu auth --credential client_secret.json once

servers.notes: 696 stars, Apache-2.0, pushed 2026-09-28. v0.10.10 (2026-07-25) is still the stable release on Homebrew, winget and npm (@eat-pray-ai/yutu). The newest build is the v0.11.0-rc1 prerelease (2026-09-21), and it changes things you will notice. OAuth becomes mandatory for HTTP mode, and the HTTP endpoint is pinned to localhost:8216. MCP output now defaults to JSON. The multi-agent mode is merged into a single 'Miffy' agent that accepts OpenAI-compatible providers as well as Gemini. There are also Docker images on Docker Hub and GHCR. Install first (brew install yutu), then authenticate, then run yutu mcp over stdio. The quota caveat is unchanged: videos.insert costs 1,600 units, which is about 6 uploads a day on the default 10k quota. Unverified API projects can only upload private videos until Google audits them. Lighter upload-only alternative: anwerj/youtube-uploader-mcp (50 stars).
